critical.text: After reading reviews of this I made a purchase and gave it a go. I have to say I was quite dissapointed. We played it several times and while a couple of the games did turn out quite interesting, overall, this game, in my opinion, does not compare to some of the better games out there.

A decent game, however, the math is difficult to figure out and the scoring is odd at times. Additionally, it is a very one sided game. One person is going to win and they are going to win BIG. The rivers expansion helped a litte, but unfortunately no enough to balance out play. Worth picking up if it is on sale, but don't pay full price.

I'm starting to come around a bit on this game. I still am not a huge fan, but I can at least see it's appeal to the right crowd. For the serious gamer, this is still a game you won't be suggesting much, but if you have smart, non-gaming friends this can be a solid entry for doing somthing casual with them that will engage them without being threatening. Fo...

Good game, but I am not sure why. The strategy seems haphazard and win or lose I can't seem to figure out why I win or lose. However, my family loves it and even my kids can win at this one. It's a very good family game where anyone can win. My biggest complaint is the scoring of the farmers - if there are a lot of farmer's out there it can get very complic...

This was my first 'designer' game and it was good enough for me to try another: Ra. Time and a few plays, though, have left me rather disappointed in Carcassone and still eagerly playing Ra. Some interesting variants spice it up a little bit, but I now only play this game with absolute non-gamers to introduce them to the hobby.

mixed.text: This is a phenomenal game that can be played easily by first timers. The random factor makes it interesting as players try to maximize their points on the board. I love the tile-laying mechanic and the fundamentally simple design of the game. But this game is also very deep. This is a game I could play every day.

I like that Carcassonne can be explained to a new player in about 10 minutes. Even for folks who aren't into tabletop games you can talk them through the mechanics of play and how to score points very quickly. This makes finding players a breeze, and Carcassonne is now on the short list of games I will bring to family get togethers for dessert and coffee ga...

The base game of Carcassone. Easy and fun to play. This is a must have for every boardgame lover and perfect as a family game ... especially when there are grown children that join in. But after a few plays things will get rather simple and possibly boring. So you'll be needing some of the many expansions to keep the fun going.

Really great gateway game and a nice way to draw in all sorts of new gamers, whether they be kids or adults. The nice thing is that with some good expansions, this can become a strategic and deep game. In my opinion, playing with the King, Inns and Cathedrals, and Traders and Builders expansions together makes for a killer, deep game, and one that with some...

Uno de los euro-juegos más clásicos y el primero que tuve en mi colección. Su simplicidad es francamente genial, se trata de una especie de una especie de híbrido entre un rompecabezas y un dominó moderno: se amontonan al principio del juego, y al azar, todas las piezas con las que se juega, cuadrados de cartón que contienen dibujos de pequeños trozos de un...

positive.text: Only played so far with two. And it is a great game for two--elegant, leisurely without dragging, involving just the right combination of strategy and luck. We sort the tiles into several piles, mixing the river tiles in with the rest, and then let them work their way to the top. Adds another difficult decision to the game.

Is a wonderful two-player game, and I'm always up for playing it. I get kind of possessive of this game though. Whenever freinds want to borrow my games, I always reserve this one as off-limits becuase I'm just so afraid they will lose one of the tile peices or loose on of my precious follower peices!

My favorite game when played with Inns and Cathedrals, Traders and Builders and a house rule with the Robber only: the Robber is awarded to the person who OWNS (NOT COMPLETES) the longest road, which entitles him/'her to one point for every completed road, usually 15-20. This increases the value of the road pieces you pull, and provides perfect balance to t...

That I say of this game... probably that are the 20€ better spent in my life. It is the first board game that I bought and from here, everything changed. Every game is different, every time you apply a strategy, every time you try to obtain more points and to excel to achieve it. I am charmed with putting tiles! ;) #----0----# Que digo de este juego... quiz...

Played 10+ Scoring is contrived and the Meeple placement is often fiddly. I enjoy this game now I am familiar with the mechanics. How well you do is more influenced by your own play than the actions of the other players. A novice or even an intermediary player can be left feeling like a spectator when playing with experts, this is not a criticism, it is a j...

critical.text: Massively over-rated, very luck based game. Fun if you don't expect strategy to be the primary factor in deciding a winner. Great for introducing non-gamers to german gaming, due to a combination of strong theme, good reference, straightforward rules and the chance for a win by even the most average player.

2001 Yeah, my first german-style-game. It's fun, it's fast and requires some thinking. The dice-randomness brings the score down a bit though. Also, it's a bit too long with 13 points (first player to 10-11 points usually wins) and it's too dificult to catch up with "lucky" players getting ahead.

Excellent game system that has fast turns and great player interaction. Everyone should have a copy in their library of games. Easy to teach new players and yet much more depth than most 'beginner' games. That said, I think I have reached Settlers burnout. For me the game simply lasts too long. As with original Risk...it is time for Settlers to retire.

Great game but too luck driven! I'm sure it is better with the expansions. Much of it is luck of the dice and having your settlement/city in the right spot to get resource cards. Without these resource cards... you are pretty much toast. Always a good time to play though! Just a lot better games out there to play. Great intro game for starting people into S...

The classic "gateway game" for people who aren't gamers. Simple enough to teach the layperson without intimidating them into quitting, and random enough that the novice has a chance against the expert. Once they play this, they'll want to see what the other games on the shelf are like. UPDATE: Not sure if it's the plethora of newer Eurogames I've been expos...

mixed.text: Great overall game, good for group interaction. Concept and strategy are very good with multiple and dynamic paths to victory. Games are usually balanced but lopsided ones happen occasionally. Dice rolling means a small luck factor, but it's strategic enough that a few bad rolls won't break you. Highly replayable. Trading aspect is interesting also and mean...

B+ Very Good Game (like to play and never will turn it down). One of the Best "Gateway Games" to get non-gamers to play games. Pretty much everyone who plays it loves it. The simple elegance of these rules is superior to the more complicated mechanics of "Cities and Knights" and "Seafarers". The only improved versions are the "Trojan War" and "Wall of China...

So, this really is a great game I must admit. I've very seldom played it, and I don't know that I regret that. "Take That" cards still annoy me to this day, but they're pretty downplayed in settlers. I definitely should give this game a few more spins. Apr 08: The elegance is finally getting to me. My thoughts wander to the simple economy and the beauty of...

These days it feels too random, but considering I haven't played any game as much as this one, and still enjoy a game now and then, this needs to be rated high. It is an absolute classic. The dice rolls can make or break your game, but there is strategy involved to mitigate some of that. This is a game that is extremely easy to teach someone and is a great...

Surprisingly replayable due to the randomness of the rolling, but enough skill of placement to maintain a feeling of controlling your destiny. The game's progression can be slow, but the turns are fast. The game almost always ends anti-climatically. It's a fun game, and one you'll be proud of winning, even if it was mainly by luck.

positive.text: The history of Catan tie-in products has been a little uneven over the years, but a number of them are great; it’s a little funny, but the line really started hitting its stride in the 2010s - about the time most hugely successful product lines would be hitting the point of “well, I guess I need a new boat”. I particularly recommend: Catan Starfarers Rise o...

So, it's a ten then. I hate to have to go with the crowd, but after several years playing, it's still one of the first games to come out during a session. Yes, there's a certain ammount of luck (I once won a game becuase the dice simply WOULD NOT stop coming up 4's. Guess who had 4) but it's usually up to the individual players as to what use they make out...

The best game invented in the last decade. With the changeable tileset and the trading system you don't get hardly boring. Also the subject reponds of one's desire: everyone wants to seek their fortune in the unexplored world. We've played once with ten players with two games and a 5&6 player expansion. Great fun.

I am so glad this game exists. Fun. It's for the random folks who game. Playable with folks who want to be gamers, but really like a bit more light fare. The dice are the deciding factor. I sware.. put everything on 9, it's better than 6/8 in our games :). It reminds me of gambling a lot. Hard if there is someone who gets seriously.. painfully beaten each t...

Probably the best and most balanced four player game ever. Settlers defines simplicity in game play, which leads to wins by more than a few folks new to the game over more established players. The mechanics are a blend of sheer dumb luck, careful strategy, and some real good smak. I am the sheep king...baaaah........

critical.text: Played and was left wondering what the big deal was, especially when compared to Lord of the Rings at its best. It felt like a lot of the experienced people saying, "do this, so we can do this other thing." Might be good to play as a family game, but otherwise seemed too light, without a lot of meaningful decisions to make.

This game, while crazy popular on the Geek right now, is just "okay" in my book. I've only played it twice, and while it was a fun exercise in cooperation, the game didn't really hook me in. I'm sure we'll play it a few more times, then it may sit and gather dust for a while. Update: Traded away after four plays.

I'm a little surprised at how popular this one is. Like small world, I just don't get it. It seems to fall pretty flat to me. The problem is there is little tension in the game and all of the other players really aren't necessary. You could just as easily play this game solo with all of the pieces yourself, since there is little independent action-taking. L...

Terra has a similar theme plus a tension between acting in your own interests or playing cooperatively, Shadows Over Camelot has the traitor. Both would have been much less fun as purely cooperative games. Pandemic is a purely cooperative game. Pandemic models the spread of disease quite well and generates some tension through the infection and epidemic car...

Update after a few solo games on iOS As a solo game (which, for me, is the only way most cooperative games should be played), this rates at least a 6. ---- A quick-playing cooperative game. Sometimes it's quick because it's impossible to solve! A fun activity, but more like a group puzzle than a game. It has the same silly rule as Lord of the Rings: players...

mixed.text: Smooth and slick game that requires a lot of communication to maximise efficiency. Challenging, but not to the point it is frustrating. Hits the sweet spot of being easy to learn and difficult to master. Great theme too. Excitement 7.5 Strategy 8 Interaction 8 Balance 7 Replay-ability 9 Theme 8 Components 7.5 Value 7.5 Time investment 9 Player Downtime 8

Tried it twice so far, had a great time. It is a fast cooperative game which is an A in my book. Only criticisms so far are that some roles are more active than others, and that 'hive mind' strategies seem to be ideal. Edit - played it several times recently, each more enjoyable than the last. Previous criticism still applies, though I have more appreciatio...

Purely cooperative endeavor. There is no room for contention here. Each player plays a unique roll that must leverage the rolls of the other players to succeed. The play is tense as disease continues to spread. There are ways to adjust the difficulty of play to suit the group you are playing with.

I think my biggest complaint about the base game is that I just do not enjoy it with only 2 players. My favorite feature about co-op games is the discussion and strategy planning. It just isn't as much fun with only two players, but this is just me. I know a lot of people love this game with only 2 players, and if I did, I would definitely rank it higher.

What more can be said about this modern classic? For me this provides a pure and puzzly cooperative experience. I really like it as a 2 player game, and it is perfect for an evening with a good friend. I don't feel the need to pull this one out when meeting up with my bigger gaming circle, but for those family/few-friends at home nights it is perfect. I thi...

positive.text: Hands down my favorite new game of BGG CON 2007. We played it 5 times in a row -- it's just that good. Too bad Pandemic won't be in stores until January of 2008. If you like pure coöp games (Lord of the Rings, Feurio, etc.), this should be right up your alley. Having 5 roles to choose from gives the game some extra variability. Also, once you get good you c...

I tend to either love or easily tire of co-op games. Pandemic joins Knizia's LoTR as my favorite true co-op. It edges LoTR out merely in time to set-up and play. LoTR can be an undertaking to explain enough details so that players enjoy their first time through the game, while Pandemic is fast enough that even if the players don't quite get everything that...

This is an amazing co-op game. I play mostly with my wife and this is a game that I can't really imagine getting tired of. Win or lose, I usually want to play again immediately. On the Brink and the fan-made expansion from on ArtsCow add much more variety and good game play, only enhancing an already great game.

Hey! I can finally rate this game I've been playtesting on and off for a couple years. I really like Pandemic, it's the best cooperative game I've played since Lord of the Rings. The key is in the pacing; the game successfully ratchets up the tension as infections spread and outbreaks pop up all over the place, and the players fight a race against time to c...

When this game first came out I followed it closely. I even listened to a Google Talk that the designer of the game gave. Honestly, I didn't get it. I couldn't tell if it was just another one of these co-ops that ends up being *essentially* "Go Fish" (e.g., Lord of the Rings, Shadows over Camelot). Also, there were reviewers who were writing that every play...

critical.text: This game fills a very unique niche: an easily explainable card drafting game that scales beautifully from 3 - 7 players. The game time doesn't even increase dramatically with a higher number of players due to the simultaneous nature of the game play. Sounds great, right? For a lot of people it is, the game is already rated 73 and it hasn't even become avai...

It is awesome that this will easily accommodate 6 or 7 players, but to be frank while I like it I prefer Fairy Tale. Other than the occasional glance at another player's tableau, I didn't feel like the drafting mattered much. What's left, then, is the card play itself, which is slightly more engaging but pretty simple and dry. There's also a serious problem...

Bland bland bland. I'm basically done with this after 7 plays spread over 6 months. Those 7 plays are virtually indistinguishable from each other, nothing memorable in a single one of them. Choose a card, put it on the table 18 times, add up the scores. Ooh, 42 this time, instead of 48. Wow. edit: Ended up purchasing this, mostly just to get some use out of...

7 Wonders was a game that I initially found very attractive. Unfortunately, the decisions ended up being trivial enough with long term play that I ultimately reached the point where I was no longer interested in playing it further. I wrote a review of it, though I largely no longer agree with my own conclusion:

I don't know how to categorize this game. It's somewhat like a light Race for the Galaxy or Glory to Rome, yet there does seem to be a little more interaction. Not as 'solitaire' as I expected or heard it to be. A good game that plays very quickly. May get tiresome after a while, but plays in so short a period of time and accommodates up to 7, so may be a k...

mixed.text: I was very wrong about this game. My first few plays of this popular card-drafting game fell flat, but I like Duel and once the app came out, realized how great this game is. With my newfound appreciation and the great things I hear about the expansions, this game is sure to rise next year.

Well designed game that plays fast, offers just enough differentiation in strategies and has very good art. It's easy to teach, the only difficult concept is trading for resources, some people struggle to understand what that really means. The base game mains a level of simplicity that makes the game approachable for everyone and playable in a half an hour....

Fun at first then it becomes repetitive. The drafting mechanic is nice, every time your strategy changes but in few games you will try them all. It is more fun to play against advanced players, but then again, there are other games. Looking forward to try it with expansions. Update: After playing more games with experienced players I raised the rating from...

Nagyon érdekes, elég egyedi mechanikájú játék. A kártyák miatt van a szerencsének is szerepe, főleg több játékos esetén, de azért jól lehet benne kombinálgatni. A grafikák gyönyörűek, a kártyákra kell egy védő, mert nem annyira bírják a strapát. Egyetlen hibája talán, hogy a működés és a téma viszonya nem túl szoros. Nem nagyon tudom beleélni magam abba, ho...

I can still play this game for two reasons: it's fast and pretty. As a game though I find it uninspiring. The length and the mechanic do not allow much room for changing/adapting strategy during the game, so you're basically taking chances as you can't forsee when and if you're going to see certain cards. Also there is really not much in the way of interact...

positive.text: An excellent card game with simple mechanics and a fast pace to it. Very convenient in that it plays a crowd (in about 40 minutes, no matter how many play) and stands up well to repeat performances. The game is tricky to explain and I could see it at times not hitting the table because I can't muster the energy to teach it. "Race for the Galaxy" suffers fro...

Fast paced and hugely rewarding game, in which the game develops extremely quickly. If you aren't watching your near neighbours closely and other opponents at all then the game can evolve without enough time to combat others, or remove critical choices from them. The choices are endless and there are many paths to collect points to win the game. I love card...

Bam! Easy 10. Scales perfectly well from 3 - 7. It really does only take 30 minutes and there is plenty of strategy. --- How is this game not #1? It's easy to teach, fast to play, engaging for all skill levels --even us hardcore mega-gamers, and more versatile than anything out there. Best with 3, 4, 5, 6, or even 7! I should stop buying other games and jus...

I'm sure this is a game that will improve once we know the various cards and chains. UPGRADE. I like playing 7W quite a bit, but teaching it is a real bastard. UPGRADE. This could be the perfect game. Fast, fun, strategic, tactical, luck, free will, and smack talk. And short enough to play over and over.

I love that it scales well for 2-7 players. There just aren't many games that you can play with more than 5 players. This fills a nice niche in the game collection. I also really like shorter time length (30-45 min). Now with a baby crawling around, we can still get a couple games in after she has gone to bed.

mixed.text: The deckbuilding game that blew up the industry and like many was my first introduction to the mechanic. I like that the base game is really easy to learn and the fast pace of the game, in addition to the mechanic of balancing your deck with valuable but useless victory point cards, but the theme is really lacking for me and so my interest has waned.

Cool game, I see what all the hype is about now. After having some rough plays with Race for the Galaxy (boring) I was worried that Dominion wouldn't live up to the hype either; however, my g/f and I were pleasantly surprised at this new mechanic of deck building during gameplay.

Still the best deck builder. Other games might add more fluff and mechanisms but if I want a pure deck builder in a tight package, Dominion is where I go. I can easily spend an afternoon just playing this with friends over and over again. It never gets old. === Promos: Black Market,Envoy,Governor, Stash Exp: Alchemy,Cornucopia,Dark Ages,Guilds, Hinterlands,...

A good medium weight card drafting type game. The back story really doesn't influence play that much. It's very fast paced and mixing in certain decks allow for player interaction (attacks). Have taught and played with about 16 different people, all have highly enjoyed it except 1 so I'd say those are good odds this will be a crowd favorite.

(-) The dynamic of shuffeling and card picking distracts you a bit from pure gaming. Some times better online. (+) The variety of strategies available and at the same time the great doses of luck involved. And of course the huge lot of expansions! The basic box is without doubt a must have.

positive.text: [167 plays] Boy this is fun! If I get sick of this after 500 games, I don't care, because those first 499 games will have been worth the ride. I like efficiency/economic games, and this is a clever little beast which plays quite quickly after you have a couple of games under your belt. Building your deck and getting your engine running, then converting from...

I feel like we (personally) haven't even begun to scratch the surface of the variety in this game, and there's a large expansion on the way! We're still messing about with the suggested setups from the rulebook! This is such a clever and original design. A game like this comes along once in a decade.

The unbelievable amount of hype/buzz for this game prepared me to be disappointed, but so far I really enjoy this game. The quick play time and large amount of replayability are huge assets. There is just the right amount of luck, but skill seems to play a big enough role that the better player should win most of the time. The theme is, like many releases,...

Dominion is just like that. I love the feeling of bui...

mixed.text: Solid worker placement game but possibly supplanted by Caverna, which is almost everything that Agricola is but with more stuff. What Agricola does offer (that Caverna doesn't) is a much tighter and harder game (avoiding starvation is harder) and more variation between games (the job cards you can choose from are drawn from a deck).

They don't call this Misery Farm for nothing. But, I have so much fun being miserable. The game defines how worker placement should work, has amazing tactile progress as you build your farm and is agonizingly hard to figure out. The only knock I would give it is that it feels like it ends just as you are finally building something to be proud of.

I typically play with card-drafting, a la Fairy Tale.

(And yes, the buildings can be very powerful.) And yet the...

Best game ever played! Great balance, awesome mechanics, good theme, lotsa ways to win and countermeasures, learnable in 10 minutes but sooo deep. The perfect resource management game. A gamer's game--yet all my smart friends love its depth and perfect balance. All the hyperbolic praise this game gets is totally earned. Play it! Buy it!

There is a one-time reading/discussion of the rules which lasts about an hour due to the manual being long and poorly written (english). After the rules are understood, the game is awesome! One of the favorites of our gaming circle. gaming circle regards it as one of our favorites

This game has a tremendous amount of charm while you're in the process of learning all its ins and outs, and it is standing up brilliantly to an unprecedented number of repeated playings. It's great how all the small decisions add up to such a rich variety of sequences of events. Ride the tide of opportunity.

positive.text: This is my favorite game outside of the Pandemic Legacy games. The birds are beautiful, building a bird engine is fun, the boards explain how to play so I can get someone started fairly quickly, and the amount of cards makes it very replayable. Not much player interaction though which has it falling on my list of favorites. Still, a beautiful, peaceful game

Really great game! I enjoy this game a lot. I guess you get to be a bird grower. You play bird cards in 4 different regions (using food to play them). Hatch eggs, draw new cards. mixed.text: My favorite game for 5-7 player counts. Action and resource management with a great theme and good solo experience. One of the best games to play with seven players and offers a great evening of engaging game play every game. The Fenris expansions offers a nice storyline and opens up some more gameplay options once unlocked.

Unas ilustraciones espectaculares y una producción excepcional hacen de este buen juego una maravilla. Muy recomendable para todos los públicos, siempre que sepan a qué están jugando.

Great game overall, but one that didn’t transition into an evergreen. Masterpiece in action selection + engine building. Although not the epitome or even apotheosis of engine building, a singularity in various engines intertwining and interacting w/ one another. With this much fuzz about the game I had to try it. I'm a big fan of party games (laughs are more important as tactical decissions), but I don't really like "word"-games, so it was with a little bit of mixed feelings. I enjoyed the game, but it really isn't my kind of game unfortunately. In the genre I prefer games like Spyfall or One Night Werewolf.

mixed.text: Much better game with 6 than 4, as you have team discussions, and the other team can put people off. Would happily play again with 6, but not gain with 4. Different type of social party game, a keeper (Rating 7.783, Dec 2015). UPDATE: Pub Meeple Ranking Engine Dec 2020 (Rating: 7.928).

Really enjoyable party game which pretty much anyone can play. The best thing about this game is that you can play this as competitively as you like. For example, in a particular group you can easily alter the rules to allow only 2+ word hints etc. Really fun. Would happily play pretty much in any group.

The spymaster role in this game is extremely important & demanding: if the spymaster cannot think of multiple word clues and only gives a clue for "one" word at a time: the game kind of falls apart because it is stupidly easy. So the game requires smart, creative spymasters. When there are good spymasters the game is addictive & fun: it is the kind of game...

The game feels like it's been out there for decades (one of those "how come this game wasn't a thing before" experiences). It can be frustrating at times, but when it works, it works wonderfully. + Duet (which is an interesting coop version that is a bit more unforgiving and frustrating at times)

To be the spymaster is really fun. You look at all The words and try to find a connection between them. It's fast and simple but so clever and fun. I would rate it even better if it was even more fun to be the team mates to The spy master. But still, The best party game I've ever played.

Wonderful, wonderful! Challenges Celebrities as the best word/party game ever. It's a thoughtful game with exactly four players, but more of a wild ride of a party game with six, eight or even more players, as you get to hear some interesting and downright entertaining discussion! We also enjoy the two- and three-player co-op versions.

You watch people staring at the board for minutes on end trying to optimize how to spend $107 and then asking for confirmation that he added everything up correctly. Or trying to figure out how much oil, coal etc to buy so that you have X dollars left...

Every play of this game is too similar. I liked it the first time out but then realised on subsequent playings that it deceptively makes you think there is lots in it when really there isn't. Bland auction game. Though I have moved my rating up because I might be convinced to play it again even though I don't really care to.

Hmm. There is a lot that I like about this game. I like the tile placement elements of making connections and "blocking", the supply-demand model with the resources, and the resource management challenges. What I dislike is the endgame. You can manage to have a ton of cash to do what you need to win, but ONLY if a useful powerplant gets put out during your...

It also means instead of 3 phases in the original, too often the has extremely short 2nd & 3rd phases, because players have enough income to build to several cit...

Just my sort of game - bit of bidding, bit of player interaction, lot of planning and a little bit of hidden information (power plants). Currently one of my favourites - interesting to see if it holds up to repeated plays - if it doesn't the rating will fall ** Update, well it has (down from 9 to 8), not played it for a while and I've stopped actively looki...

mixed.text: Good game. The rules are are probably some of the worst written I ever read. The game is fairly simple if you get it explained by someone who knows how to play. Not one of my absolute favourites because it is slightly fiddly and a little long (2 hours). However it hits the table again and again, so it has qualities.

A game that I very much enjoy playing, but find a little bit clunky in terms of the mechanics and the amount of work that players need to do in order to make it work. The importance of getting the right power plants seems to overwhelm the other decisions (resources/map), and the 'luck of the draw' can leave players stranded with nothing much to do in the la...

After a few plays, I have come to view this game as fun, but certianly not the best auction game around. While it will play 6 player, I now feel that not everyone has the ability to win. Generally there are only 2 of 6 players who actually have a shot of winning and everyone else just seems to come up short.

Aaargh! A game I hate to love. Balance, smooth gameplay and surprising magnetism and replayability. Problem is once more the theme. I mean it's great *yawn* to provide electricity *yawn* to Germany, Benelux and whatnotties *yawn* and power is media-sexy. Yeah, *yawn* this game is the it for anyone looking for a light-medium weight euro to electrify their so...

------------------------------------ Expansions: Northern Europe & UK, Korea & China, Brazil/Spain & Portugal Awesome game, and with the Stonemaier treasure chest has a great look and feel to it. Definitely going to be ending up with most/all of the maps eventually for this ^^. ------------------------------------

positive.text: Still my highest-rated game, both in the original edition and the remake. When played with a group of players who really know how to play this game, it's incredibly competitive and tons of fun. When played with some folks who don't know "how to play well" there can be a runaway leader problem sometimes (depending on the power plants that come up). Aweseome...

As a big fan of 18xx games, I tend to like the heavyweight, theme-rich, German offerings such as Die Macher. This game fits into that category and gives the same grand feel of running a major nationwide operation. The rules are actually much easier to learn than expected. How best to spend your money is the hard part. After just one play of this game, I am...

Great auction, building game. Improved in this edition which is a bit easier to play (the old version you were fighting the game for the first half hour) and shorter. Wonderful gaming experience as the game unfolds like a novel with an ending that is almost always worth the wait.

Wonderful, wonderful game. Played twice with 3 then 4 players. This game has already shot up to be one of the best that I own. We just finished a game and I'm already yearning to start another one. Can't stop thinking about what I would do next time. Lots of thinking, lots of strategies. All without the paralysis analysis problem. My best buy of the year.

One of my favorite games -- I loved it so much I spent a lot of time and money building better components for it. Check out my PS and PDF downloads. Hmm, they changed the entry -- my rating and comment is for Funkenschlag (the original version). I feel that Power Grid takes everything great about Funkenschlag and trashes it.

You either roll them or you don't, that's it. For me, too much luck and too few choices. The other half of the die was some numbers that seemed like red herrings, too hard to g...

Oh yeah, for a Yahtzee type game it's okay. Some decisions to be made and the usual dice angst. They've mixed card abilities into the mix, which is a nice idea, but unlike To Court the King there's not much of a power buildup. Player elimination isn't a problem because the game is quick, but with big groups I'd rather play Coup or The Resistance. Still look...

I was unexpectedly impressed with the "damage many others" mechanic: Those monsters inside Tokyo damage those on the outside, and vice versa. And if you want to flame out and take 2-3 other inhumanoids with you - knowing that you won't last another round - you can. That's a thing of beauty. This would be an instant purchase at $15-20. But it's a "nevermind"...

Obviously a very random game. Not a deep strategy game at all. Just a fun light hearted game. Certainly something to be played with children, or as a fun way to end the night. Not a lot of meaningful decisions to be made -- just chuck the dice and do what you can. Still, pretty good for what it is.

Good, quick, dice chucker with an endearing theme. I'll probably keep it around to fill that gap in my collection. Its biggest value is that it can be played by young and old. I use a variant I created called . It doubles the number of energy cubes you get from an energy roll, essentially getting more cards into play much quicker. This makes the game much m...

mixed.text: The theme of this game really fits into its game mechanics combining the luck of the dice and the deck of cards. The designer was perfect in every way to bring about the concept of dominating Tokyo by different monsters and the art used can appeal to a kids and adults as well. However, the Kaiju theme does not appeal to some people. If the people you're pla...

Just a fun, dumb, dice rolling w/ability to purchase cards to enhance powers. If rated just based on how fun and quick it is, it should be an 8.5 to 9. Roll through the ages is a better dice rolling for combinations to get points/achievements game . . . this is way simpler yet more fun and doesn't drain your brain

Originally bought so I could stop playing Sorry and Battleship with my nieces and nephews. Most of the kids love it, and its so much more fun than the traditional kids board games. My adult friends love it too, a great "Family" game but gets lots of play on Grown ups game night too. Check out My card reference sheet in the "files" section to clarify all the...

Great family game... it can be the perfect gateway game to introduce non-gamers to gaming... it's light, fun and has very cool components... And with the expansions adding more to the core gameplay with evolutions and new powers making the game also appealing to gamers It's a game for everyone

Of the games I own, there is no game that is more popular. It is easy to learn, and almost anyone I play with loves the game. positive.text: I dislike games that paste a theme onto existing games, and was afraid this would be Yathzee in disguise. I couldn't have been more wrong! This is a quick game of ridiculous face stomping, energy gathering and getting points. Turns go fast, and the upgrade cards add a great diversity to the game. Great filler game!

2019 Still a beloved game, now playable with 2 kids ages 4 and 5 who understand nearly all the rules and options. Only slight modifications like curating the power cards to be easier cards. I don't mind throwing in some variants like: 1) Start with 10 points and 8 health 2) If you claw, you must enter Tokyo 3) Everyone drafts/draws a power to start; start w...

Best filler game I 've played so far. Simple, easy with tons of fun. You can never say no to bringing this game out since it plays fast, has light strategy and although it is a dice game, it's not all push your luck. I think everyone that I 've played with enjoyed it and had a great time. What more can you ask in a filler?

I haven't given this game a fair shake yet, only one two player game with my 8 y.o. Looking forward to some more plays.EDIT: Played two five player and one four player game. Obviously, it's much better. Decisions felt more meaningful an...

I really enjoy push-your-luck dice games and you couldn't have a better theme on top of such a mechanism, King of Tokyo is a match made in heaven! The game looks fantastic. mixed.text: Fun light engine building game. Really easy to teach to new and seasoned gamers alike. You can definitely see why it was a nominee for the Spiel this year. *edit* I took this to the family for Christmas along with other games. This was the one game that my uncles were really keen on. It says something when people ask you where they can get their copy.

One of my personal favorite gateway games to introduce to new board game players. Great component quality, fun gameplay; simple and easy to understand. It is very similar to Century: Spice Road but I personally think both can be in your collection. Splendor is the right game to play in under an hour, and can be played with any players at any skill level.

The rules are extremely simple and i play it regularly with gf in 2 player mode and it works quite well. The material is really awesome and I really enjoy to play this game once in a while. The strategy is not incredible and you need to consider this as a light game. Since I continue to play it regularly I consider it as a good game

Simple to learn and teach others. Not a ton of diversity in the nobles, but enough that each game plays out slightly differently. I wish there was slightly more diversity in the artwork, but the quality of the components is quite high, making this game worth the money you'll spend.

Via chip-collecting and card development you try to get wealthier to increase your prestige (15 prestige points wins). Splendor is an ingenious game because of guiding choices you have to make each turns. Splendor's game play is excellent because of the limited amount op options (3) you have each turn.

A great gateway game which is perfect for 2 players. Easy to learn, fun to play. The theme is not that bad and I'd even say this is not that abstract as many of you say. With 4 players I'd say this game gets a bit random, especially with people who tend to take the first player penalty a lot.

I have the "mini" version for traveling - and the game is very fun to play! There is only one minor design flaw - the bag, which can't be closed properly and is too big for traveling purposes. But I don't really care. Verdict: A very good game, but as it is pretty abstract it will not be in my all-time favorite list.

Quick, brainy and entertaining game, that can deliver a very fun experience in about half an hour. The interaction is on point. The scoring system is a little confusing at first but not difficult. While seemingly simple on the surface, Azul holds significant depth and strategy and packs that in a beautiful, well illustrated and put together box. Each game holds surprising depth and the nature of the game ensures that each time you play will be different and end up with a beautiful player board.

positive.text: Beautiful tiles. Enjoyable abstract. I like that the game is as much about outthinking your opponents as playing your own board. Definitely keep an eye on what tiles other players need, and factor that into your tile selection. Great tactical strategy about when to select tiles from the middle to change the order of who may get stuck with leftover tiles at...

Azul is a fantastic tile drafting game where players aim to complete rows and columns of certain tiles, gaining points for adjacency planning. It is just forgiving enough to the point where decisions are difficult and need to be planned ahead, but if a plan doesn't go through, it is easy enough to shift and aim for another color or row in future rounds. Azul is the epitome of everything I love about Kiesling's games. He is my favorite designer. Azul is so simple to remember all the rules, teach the rules, and get to the table. Yet everyt...

I was not convinced of this game, but with how great Century is I decided to take a chance on this one too. So much crammed in to about 45 minutes, I wish I could have played i...

Loving this so far. My wife asked me unprompted to play this one, which she rarely does. My 8 y.o. saw us playing and joined us for our next game. Beautiful production. Quick playing. critical.text: Much later, I have finally tried this. I can see there is a lot here. San Juan on steroids. But it is not for me. Not a knock on the game, I can see how it might rate extremely high for some. But for me, I'm not interested in learning the game well enough to find the depth that is obviously present.

I think I'm done with this. My first impression was that despite the massively confusing symbols it was a game I would probably grow to love. So I gave it some more chances, and now I'm up to 5 plays. The symbols still being a pain might just be my own deficiency, but more problematic is that there's just no spark in this game, there's nothing but spinning...

I am beginning to think Tom's designs aren't for me. I thought the effects in this game were less interesting than San Juan. I am also not sure that I like the blind action selection, as it adds a mind reading element that does not seem to add much. Finally, the art, while attractive does not convey any meaningful information, and sort of distracts from wha...

Rating based on 25-30 plays thus far; it's a game I will play if others suggest but rarely will I recommend or push it myself. The game seems overly complex for what it is -- a luck-based card game -- and frankly, I'd rather play San Juan or Dominion, where the cards are easier to understand and the game a bit more intuitive. The only unique element here is...

After one play, I'm not sure how to rate this. I think the visuals are confusing as hell, and the whole thing feels a lot more like adding cogs to a machine than "playing a game." Theme is non-existent (does anyone really feel like they're building a space empire here?), which doesn't help matters. I didn't have any FUN while playing this. I'll try it again...

mixed.text: Really good experience of a game. The difficult thing is to get used to the symbols and how the intermingle. But when you do that you start rolling. Try reading the name of the card before you play it, look at the picture and after a while you really feel you are making a space empire.

I really like the speed at which this game plays. There is almost no down time and once you have learnt all the fiddly icons a game can finish in 30 mins. Re-playability is extremely high. Only down side is there is little player interaction, however the first expansion offers blank cards which can easily fix this issue with your own house rules and creativ...

A very fun "tableau-building game". I guess that is what you would call it? Because there are two end game scenarios (get all victory points from pool or somebody builds a 12-card tableau), it really does feel like a race. You are trying desperately to see a strategy come to fruition while at the same time constantly re-evaluating your situation due to the...

Really fluid empire building game with cards. If you like games where you create the engine that pumps your hand full of cards (resources), this is the game for you. The game icons take a while to get used to but in the end they make sense and are easy to read. The game is daunting to teach for new players especially if they are not used to this kind of gam...

A great card game that I would describe as an engine-builder. It plays great a 2p, which is important to me. I think there is a lot of depth out of a small box. I have purchased the first three expansions (waiting for two of them to arrive) to try more content. I think it plays pretty quick and has a neat mechanism where each player picks the action they wa...

positive.text: A deeper offering than San Juan, but using some of the same basic mechanics. The added depth is a true enhancement rather than pasted-on extra complexity, and works seamlessly within the system. The theme and mechanics meld together far better here than in San Juan, and the new layers of strategy are a delight. The artwork is gorgeous. Now firmly ensconced...

It's really unbelievable how well tuned the designer has made this game. Brilliant in 2 player, great in 3 and 4 player. Great choices. I have to dock a half point for the wonky iconography and icon color picking, but once you've learned it, it really does make the game play faster.

Race for the Galaxy is a great example of how to craft a solid game based on snowball economies and optimisation: add extensive doses of deduction. Each turn players simultaneously and secretly choose an action. All players have access to the same pool of actions, and the one who picks each of them perform it with a bonus, but the rest of the players will b...

I love this game, if only I could find enough other people to share this love, but the symbol barrier is a bit high on this one, I tried to explain it to my group and I was so energetic and involved in my explanation that it wasn't until after I was done that I looked up and was greeted by a table full of black stares, perhaps next time. Maybe it's because I just recently started playing the original Ticket to Ride, but I'm not impressed with the Europe game. I'd rather play the original. The ferries and the tunnels just don't strike me as good ideas; more like just a gimmick to justify an expansion, or something 'different' for people who are tired of the original. I'd rather have a second...

Haven't played Ticket to Ride. I was positively suprised by this one. I was expecting a boring and slow moving game, but found a fast and tense game. Plays pretty well with any number of players. My complaints are that the theme feels rather pasted on and that the luck factor in this is immense.

At first I enjoyed the extra rules in TTE:Europe, but after several plays I miss the simplicity of the original. This is my gateway big board game in my collection, and I won't play much unless I'm introducing new folks to the hobby. It isn't a bad game, but the set collection gets repetitive to me.

Like the original, the production quality is great, the rules are simple but offer lots of opportunities to make decisions, and it's just the right length. The only issue I really have with it are the addition of train stations. They make it much harder to screw over your opponents, thus decreasing the interaction (or at least, the players' effect on each o...

mixed.text: I like the added complexity that the tunnels & ferries provide in this version. The added option of the train stations not only provide a nice out when trying to complete an impossible ticket but also add a new layer of strategy because they can give you an easy way of completing tickets at a cost of only 4 victory points. Nice addition!

A great game for light session, one of the games my game group often request to play, its kinda appealing for new gamer also... I like the game for its simple quick fun games, and decide to buy the expansion for more depth. Too bad the stations doesnt encourage route blocking, maybe need to remove them for low count of players. This TTR is good for 4 or 5 p...

On paper, equally as fun and satisfying as the original, but the layout of the board and the little bits of extra rules make it a bit less welcoming than the USA map. That's a fun change in some ways, but also works against what was the original's greatest strength of accessibility. Is a more cutthroat Ticket to Ride really needed?

Aporta un punto mas de complejidad que la versión de america, pero aliviando la tensión con las estaciones, con lo que queda todo el mundo contento.

positive.text: A classic game improved greatly by the introduction of the stations, which can offer a lifeline near the end of the game. The tunnels require an extra element of planning when going for routes as you may have to pay up to 3 cards more. I'd recommend it to anyone who enjoyed the first version of this game and those who haven't played it at all.

The latter two became two of my favorite games to be released in the last year, whereas Gloomhaven was my most disappointing game. I can see why someone might like this game. I don’t understand how this is poised to become...

TL;DR A surprisingly dull game, with a too-long setup. It's fine, but I wouldn't ask for another game. I usually wait until ten plays before rating a game, but Gloomhaven is a game I expect not to play much again, if at all, so I'm going to write down my thoughts while they are fresh in my mind. First, a caveat: I played the game in the random dungeon crawl...

Gloomhaven is an incredibly ambitious game, and a bit of a beast. It's a legacy RPG dungeon crawl, but it distinguishes itself from other similar campaign or one-off skirmish games with the sheer quantity of content (it has 95 distinct scenarios and roughly 1,700 cards), card driven mechanics, sense of progression, and story elements. I tend to dislike most...

mixed.text: The board game I didn't realize that I've been waiting for almost 30 years to be made. Playing solo gives me the same kind of feeling I had reading the Fighting Fantasy series of books as a kid. The mechanics have a steep learning curve, but are great once you get into the swing of it. Leveling the city and your characters is satisfying, as are the permanen...

Good, not excelent, but one needs to respect the time put into developing this game. I have yet to encounter a scenario that doesn't feel very well playtested and well designed. I can easily understand why this is #1 in BGG. It grows on you as you play the campaign, so buy this only if you are thinking playing the campaign. One off games are just meh.

Received via Kickstarter (finally) on 12/6/17. What a beast. A little fiddly with a fair amount of upkeep, but great gameplay. Mostly cooperative but slightly competitive makes it interesting; Fantastic components, incredibly generous. Easily the best dungeon crawler I have ever played. 1-3 terrible 4-6 ok, mediocre 7-9 good-great 10 amazeballs Set-Up (20%)...

It’s great fun for sure, yes, but, it can get a bit repetitive, the dungeons can start to feel all the same, the monsters can start to feel all the same, it’s really just hours of fun tactical puzzle combat... cool characters absolutely, but, I think I do need more “adventure” and a bit less “optimizing” in my fantasy adventure games...

I don't think its "normal" for most gamers to experience all of this game has to offer. I like playing the campaign and sometimes just playing a challenging scenario to see if I can pull it off by using some combo I've thought up in my head. This is a brilliant 1 of a kind design. The closest game I could relate it to would be mage knight, but that doesn't...

Kickstarted. Standee version. Owned expansion : Forgotten circles WOW. I can't emphasize enough how amazing this game is. Best game of 2017 for me, hands down. This is like a dream come true, I couldn't have asked for better. If you like Legacy games and dungeon crawls... please make yourself a gift and get this. You cannot not play this! #1 BEST Dungeon cr...

After play testing this game early in the development I can say that it has come a long way and well worth getting. There is high replay value in this game and endless adventures that make it worth every penny spent. And the unique gameplay is unlike anything out there so you will not be playing the different version of some other game.

Damn, I love this game (So much). Coop wasn't my cup of tea, but this one is an exception. I love how players plan their turns, initiative orders, hand management, character progressions, enemy AI, the campaign and story line, the theme and illustrations, various characters with different play styles, retirement and deck building element in the game. Defini...

Fantastic card-based dungeon-crawl campaign game. Isaac Childres has crafted what so many gamers have been looking for: a true fantasy campaign system. There's story. There's character progression. The world is alive. Skirting a 10 rating. Yes there are some "legacy" elements, but I'll gladly replay this again just with the minor permanent alterations

First STOP comparing this game to PR. Any similarities to the role-choice mechanic between the two games is purely superficial. In addition to the private nature of the choice, there is the more important idea that only one person performs each role per round. Also, the number of real choices is more limited. Regardless of your role, there are only four pos...

Update: Oct. 16th, '09: Bought it a couple weeks ago and I've been loving it. Would rather play with 4 or 5 since it's one role each, but 2 or 3 players with 2 roles each is still fun. An 8.5 right now. June 2020: Donated to GHS...

despite only 2 plays, I think this might be my favorite of the "hidden role" games. Citadels presents the players with tough choices that directly relate to the hidden role mechanic. It works great. *Update* More p...

The rules are quite straight-forward, so you can start a game quite quickly. There could have been more variation in the available buildings (filling a city with three castles, two palaces and a few churches just seems silly) and I do not particularly like the artwork (inconsistent style: realistic mixed with fantasy-like, and humans look pretty awkward). A...

Citadels by 2-8 players A race to build a city. Medieval fantasy setting. Best with 2-4 players. Becomes more chaotic and slow with more players added. Apr 2, 2014 note: recently played 2-player game. Played very similar to the 3-player. Very enjoyable! A very interactive tactical game, with lots of second guessing what your opponents shall do next, mostly...

Feels like a combination of 7 Wonders, Love Letter, and a little bit of Dominion. Like Dominion, the gameplay is fairly, but its depth is found in the variety in the role abilities and district cards. Best with fewer players as turn time can get bogged down with higher player counts.

positive.text: This game is spectacular in that it's easy to learn the general gameplay, but very difficult to master. The psychology behind determining who would most likely pick which character each round makes this game extremely enjoyable even after years of play. A spectacular game to introduce non-gamers to German Games.

What can I say it's a 10! My wife complains that it sees to much time on our table, but that's because I consider it a 10! If it came down to listing one 10 this would be it for me. I really have to give Bruno Faidutti a great amount of cudos, and thank him publicly for his accessibility.

Citadels is a very entertaining, fast-paced game. It's quite unique in that it plays well with two players up through eight. It's even better in a group of people you know well, because you can anticipate their actions and plan counter-strategies (or, try to). It's got a nice balance of some strategy and some luck.

This game is one of the first that I owned and has hit our table numerous times. Apart from the game itself there are 2 main advantages which give it a TEN. 1st it can be played from 2 to 8 people giving an extreme flexibility. 2nd it can grab ALL kind of different people, from the strategic player to the newcomer and satisfy them as one of the most interes...

I don't know what it is but this is a game that I like so much that I want to buy it again just for the pleasure of purchasing it a second time... not only that but I want to eat it! Those butterscotch golden tokens I just want to pop in my mouth! Why is this a 10? Mind you, if you play this with a dry and analytic group it can be painful, but that seems to...

critical.text: This game is surprising good, for what it is. Very few components; it's certainly a micro game. And it plays really quick, so getting eliminated isn't a big deal. And it can accommodate larger groups; but it probably shines with 3-5 people. Obviously it's quite abstract and light on the theme.

This is another card game (like Coup) where you have a very small amount of cards used to a really quick game. The premise is simple: Each player has a card in their hand. At the start of your turn you draw a card, hope you're not immediately eliminated and then choose one of your two cards to discard if you haven't been eliminated. The card you discard act...

A stupid 16-card game taking 2-3 minutes per hand of cards (a couple of won hands needed to win the game). Very random. Fun for the first couple of times. Then it becomes boring and pointless exercise. Add 1 to the rating if you play in a perfect (i.e. jolly and humour-synchronised) company Sold (a freebie in a packet with 'Hornochsen/Take 5!').

Played it twice at a friends'. Seemed a bit dry, as it was quite easy to figure out what card to play and what to keep. It is a nice filler, but nothing more. Friend made a re-themed GoT version. Greatly enhanced atmosphere, as we could get more into our roles actually. I find the game itself stays too random for me, but for a filler game I could get talked...

"Quick, portable, and inoffensive filler." What I like: - Quick, portable, minimalistic - Surprisingly interesting game for its size What I don't like: - I'm not a fan of bluffing/deduction games - Still not clear how much skill there is. Super clever game design. It's a nice quick filler, but I think it would wear out its welcome at about 30 minutes. I thi...

mixed.text: Fun and simple little card game. Not much thinking, but it's still fun to see if you will be able to win. When we went to France (May 2013), we took a copy and found we could play this game just fine while standing in line (at various museums, etc....). Recommended. Update: took my copy to disneyland in Oct 2013 to play in long lines. The rubberband broke a...

On the first few plays, people are shocked by how quickly they can get eliminated or win. One round in normal 4-player game lasts about 3 minutes. With additional plays, the subtlety and nuance of the game reveals itself: the choices you make really do matter. A great, great little microgame/filler.

Fast and Fun - This will see the table as a great filler when 4 are present haven't played with less then 4 yet ------------------ Good game though playing for the points as per the rules is a bit long with 4....we have tried the 3 points to win variant and I think I like that a bit better -

I really enjoy this little game for what it is. I think it shines best at 4 players, particularly if each player considers some higher level strategy. There is a surprising amount of depth in that deck of 16 cards for those who look. It becomes less enjoyable playing with people who don't want to work their brains a bit and strategize. They can come off fee...

This is a very quick and easy game available in many flavors (from princesses to Batman, to many others I would imagine)... but the basic mechanic remains the same. A series of cards of different rank, each with a specific ability/liability. The last player standing OR the player with the highest card wins - so the game is suitable for card-counting competi...

positive.text: What a breath of fresh air! There are so many ways this game shouldn't work. It only has 16 cards, eight of them unique. It has player elimination, often before you've even played a card. It offers few choices, let alone meaningful ones. But I've already played it 25 times, and I don't think I'm ever going to get tired of teaching it to a new group (in 30 s...

The princess is upset. Players are suitors, trying to get the palace staff to deliver your consoling love letter to the princess. Quirky Japanese game, played with a deck of sixteen cards. Each card is numbered between 1 (Guard) and 8 (Princess). There are multiple copies of several cards. One card is dealt out of the round, face down, and one card is dealt...

Very short, very neatly designed card game that plays in less than 20 minutes. Very dependant on card draw, in that you can quickly be out of a hand through one of the other players playing one of the 'gotcha!' cards, but at this super-short play time it's not an issue. ---------- The more I play this (43 plays and counting), the more I am impressed by the...

I have a difficult time giving any game a 10. But Love Letter is such a minimalist game, I have an even more difficult time finding a reason not to. It is a simple game with an easy premise that is so much fun to pick up and play with your friends. If I had any gripe at all it would be that rounds in 2 player are much too short!

Easily the best filler I own. Newbies and experienced gamers seem to like this one. It's really all about counting, but the unused card per round makes that an inexact science. There's just enough mystery and guessing to make this one surprising and replayable. Yawn at people calling Euros elegant. This is an elegant little card game. While poor bluffers ca...

critical.text: I love the theme, and at first found it great - very light-hearted, lots of joking and plenty of scope for Blackadder quotes ("Some beans and some beans is four"). But it gets old very quickly, the lack of strategy begins to grate, and very quickly it plays itself as it becomes automatic to trade the drawn beans and then give away any at the front of your h...

I've played this a few times and I'm left wondering why it is highly regarded. I think I can put it down to the fact the game is attitude dependant to make it enjoyable. I found it a little mechanically repetitive, and the trading can be a little long winded. It may benefit from once around trading like Res Publica. But Bohnanza has a bitter pill to swallow...

Our group plays this game way too politely, with everybody happily accepting cards that are clogging up everybody else's hands, so it never feels like there's any challenge to it. I suspect it might interest me more if we were more cutthroat about it, but I'd rather put energy into a different game.

I enjoyed it my few playings, but for whatever reason, I don't find it them gem that it is commonly regarded as. It is often lauded for its negotiation, but I find most of the negotiation forced (players are often desparate to get RID of a card, and usually someone wants it--if they can give something else useful in return, then that's a bonus). Perhaps if...

Finally got to play this with more than two people (3, to be exact.) It was better than with 2, since trading made sense, but it didn't seem all that much fun. Maybe we were missing something, but trades didn't seem to have much urgency -- it seemed like making trades should have been more exciting. Maybe it's better with more than 3.

mixed.text: Es un gran juego para echarte unas grandes risas y para demostrar lo perverso que es el ser humano cuando se trata de conseguir lo que uno quiere, ya que para ganar tienes que negociar con tus...amigos? Eso sí, hay tanta interactividad que como el grupo de colegas no acompañe, el juego es muy aburrido. A mi, por supuesto, me encanta!

Tactique Type: Euro Les bines n'ont jamais intéressées autant de gens! J'adore expliquer ce jeu et voir le visage des gens changer entre l'annonce des règles et le troisième tour de table. On développe rapidement une passion pour les bines ! Catégorie: Léger-Medium Thème: Fève/Bean Mécaniques: Échange et négociation Similaire dans ma collection: Sidereal Co...

A unique game by Uwe Rosenberg. I have played nothing quite like this game (until Oltre Mare, which has a similar mechanic involved). It has a very light-hearted vibe, and yet great decision making. The best aspect of Bohnanza is the negotiation and trading. Everyone ends up having fun through interaction. You find yourself helping other players to help you...

Dull, dull after you've played Oltre Mare. Too deterministic, too many regulations. More plays, and I will play it, have some fun, but I still don't really care for it. Depending on what you draw, you can have little action regarding trading, so ther can be large periods of downtime, or at least for me. EDIT: game with 4 that was much, much better. I'm fina...

Tiene una jugabilidad diferente a los otros juegos de cartas lo que tiende a que las personas que sol oquieran ganar puedan hacer trampas al cambiar el orden de las cartas, así que hay que poner mucha atención en ese sentido. Del Juego solo decir que siempre que sale a la mesa son minutos entretenidos y los margenes de victoria son cortos.

positive.text: 2 - 7 One of my oldest favorites. The strict rule of not reordering the cards in your hand adds spice. This produces a wonderful negotiation game, as it is sometimes preferable to give things away for free, or to trade at an unfavorable exchange rate. This makes it seem cooperative, but only one person can be the winner.

I always lose!!! I can't understand why... ;( Even so, the game is so addicting i don't mind losing at all, always trying to make the best out of my beans. The key is planting as much as you can outside your turn, trading your hand of beans. -update- now i'm beginning to win more often...

Still Rosenberg's best game, even after Le Havre, Ora et Labora, Agricola, and Loyang. Excellent trading game, works well with various sized groups and with both serious gamers and non-gamers. Don't play with my sister-in-law who will want 3 soy beans and 2 red beans for her coffee bean.

Perhaps my favourite game of all-time. That it's a trading game makes it very easy for newcomers to grasp (and is thus an excellent introduction to "these games of ours") as well as keeping all players involved throughout. I *strongly* recommend playing with no more than five players and removing the 4s, 22s, and 24s from the English-language version (they...

The best and most fun game in the world, a game that everyone will love from young to old, you will get laughs along the way and even name the beans after family members. A game that you can pay with your young children or your grandparents, easy to learn but hard to stop playing.. every game is different. A+A+A+A+A+A+A

critical.text: I am not sure how I feel about Dixit. I thought it would go over very well with the family, but it fell really flat. Even my wife didn't like it, which surprised me. It reminds me a lot of Apples to Apples. There is more thought and strategy in Dixit than A2A, which you would think would make it better but it makes it less fun. In other words, I feel like D...

The art is GORGEOUS and bizarre. I think it was probably worthwhile for the designer to design the game just so these cards could be published. So that part is an absolute pleasure. As for the game itself, it's one of those party games that requires you to figure out what other people are thinking, and I simply have no ability at such games. It got a little...

This falls right in between Apples To Apples and a Salvador Dali painting. As such, it's a lot better and more creative than Apples To Apples. The art is important to the game, and the creativity required is good for kids. After a couple of plays, however, the cards will certainly get old. The game plays out quickly and the expansion deck is well overpriced.

I don't think I'm good enough at abstract thinking for this game... I suck at picking topics. :( Yes, it definitely feels like visual Apples to Apples. Our first game was fun. I wonder how much longevity this game has in it... very difficult to tell, I think. I find it kind of weird that you go through the entire deck every game. I didn't like that I got to...

The board, a platform built around the perimeter of the box, and the wooden rabbit player tokens are clever. I didn't like the game very much. Everyone gets a hand of cards that have different pictures on them. The "Storyteller" chooses one of her cards and tells everyone a word, phrase, or paragraph that is supposed to hint at the picture on her card witho...

mixed.text: This game combines intelligent and innovative gameplay with beautiful aesthetics. The concept is simple: give clues about your cards, without being too specific or too vague. The reason being - you only score points if some but not all of the other players guess your card correctly. The abstract artwork allows a great deal of creativity in crafting your clu...

All the dixit games play the same only the art changes. This is a fairly fast and easy game for all ages that will test your imagination and the imagination of others. The game plays ok for three people but shines at the 5&6 player limits. If you have a wide range in ages or players that are new to gaming this is a must have.

Excellent party game!! At 6 players, the unfortunate part is that you have to reshuffle the discards and reuse some cards. However, I recommend you spread out your expansion purchases because a big part of enjoying this game is the discovery of the cards and giving diverse clues. Speaking of, the art is top notch. The surreal style but enough familiarity al...

One of my favorite party games. No subjective card judging like Apples to Apples, or Cards Against Humanity. Needed one more card pack to bring this to a good solid 8.0--and now that I got it, it really added just a little more variety, and I'm perfectly happy with my version of this game.

Este juego de verdad a mí me sorprendió, sólo usa cartas que no tienen ningún dato, ningún número ni tampoco un significado, sólo tienen una imagen. Uno debe pensar qué pensó el otro para saber por qué carta ir, es sumamente entretenido y es ideal para jugar con personas nuevas, ya que uno se demora dos minutos en explicar el juego. Totalmente recomendado.

positive.text: Dixit is certainly a party game. If you don't like party games, you won't like Dixit. Occasionally, I love a good party game, one that requires abstract thinking and creativity. Dixit is a game that lets each player's creativity shine by asking the players to see many aspects the beautifully illustrated images. Dixit requires serious out of the box thinking...

Уникальная по задумке игра. И воплощение в художественном плане отличное. Кто ищет необычность формы - приглядитесь! Негеймерская игра ("party game") с геймерским подходом. Еще: Год спустя уже не надо никого агитировать играть в Диксит. В подходящих группах продолжает играться весело и безукоризненно. Варьируем рамки и границы. Например, можно проводить тем...

first play today with 6 players. it was fantastic. works well with very concrete players and more creative. loved it. (plus: i won!) now i need the expansion! have now played with 6 and 4: superb game with 6. a very good one with 4 (we played with one card each only on the table). with 6 there was always a good competitor for the story - with 4, not so much...

Surprisingly good and definitely one of the best party games. Pure poetry! The possible associations and creative imagination of the art is limitless. Fun in a challenging way! **** To keep the game play fresh: use a theme or subject like history, geography, film, literature, sport, music, ...

Absolutely enchanting! There are very, very few party games I enjoy or games that are this light, but this is a winner! This game is simply gorgeous. The art is delightful--whimsical, dream-like, surreal, vibrant, and charmingly amateur (in a good way--it has child-like wonder and expressiveness that really goes well with the simplified figures and forms)....

First game takes some time as players need to learn all the differnt tiles but after that the game moves along fairly well even with AP prone players.

If I play more of these kind of games to have a better feel of the mechanic, rating might go up. Update: I really want to enjoy this game, but I played a little more,...

Scattershot historical events add a nice theme to this area-control game. The best history in the game is the need to match an opponent's influence in otherwise neglected regions of the world. +1 if you're old enough to know that "defect" is also a verb. Three plays, waning interest.

Wonderful system and lovely concept, but too much randomness has made me lower my rating more and more. The VP track can see tidal changes in a single turn, especially when you get too many scoring cards or your opponent gets some powerful combos such as Red Scare+Blockade, Muslim Revolutions+OPEP, and some others. Moreover, the first 3-4 turns are complete...

Ok game but not matching the strategic richness of Hannibal: Rome vs Carthage. Straightforward area control game where cards just plus or minus influence points - not very interesting. There are more interesting cards as well but many of them involve rolling 1d6 for success, which is far too random for some of the results they engender.

In many respects, the game seems to play itself. In the beginning, players typically spread out, exploring the house and collecting items and events. There are few decisions to be made. When enough of the "omen" cards have been drawn, one turns traitor. Each side then has explicit goals to achieve victory. Again, few decisions are made other than optimizing...

There's no real choices to be made anywhere, so the entire entertainment value is in the story the game creates. And that could be pretty good, I think. mixed.text: I love this game. I would actually rate it a bit higher, except for this one little problem... of the errata being almost as long as the rules. Playtesting and editing, guys. Still, if you grab the errata online, (most of it has to do with clarifications of various scenario rules), it's entirely playable, and has enormous replay value.

With as many issues as this game comes with, I still love it. There can be too many issues for serious gamers, and the balance of the haunt can easily swing in either direction depending on the situation, but in general, the balance has been put together well enough. The flavor of the game is what I enjoy more than anything. The game gets a little boring af...

Horror game im considering after I lost love for mansions of madness. Bought a cheap damaged box copy and we love it's macabre nature. Component quality isn't the best but the twist part way through the game reminds me of the film dusk till dawn with it's 2 part nature. One minute your playing the exploration find stuff game then Bang all hell breaks loose.

+ This game is a crowd-pleaser with it's thematic gameplay and it's ability to change the game with it's haunt + This game is not hard to learn which makes it a good beginner level game, but also provide fun game after game +/- If you are looking for a strategy type game than this is not it, has a lot of luck elements, but that's what makes this game fun to...

A game that doesn't take itself too seriously - and neither should you. Somewhere around the first 'Scream' movie, horror flicks started to become self-refferential, pointing out and playing off their own tropes and cliches. Betrayal follows in those footsteps, with a set of horror movie archetypes to pick from, and a setup not that far removed from a Scoob...

When the haunting kicks in, one player betrays the others, so it's a contest between the betrayer and the rest of the players. For the sake of variety, a book of scenerios is consulted at that point to find out how t...

50 games in one. I had to try a horror game with this much versatility and I wasn't disappointed. I play this game every chance I get, because no matter how many times I play it, there is always something new in it. Who is the traitor, what does he want and how do we prevent it. Even after playing it for months, I have been surprised at the ingeniuety of th...

This is definitely my favorite game (as of 6/05). The fact that you go from working together as a team to explore this house, to a betrayer vs. everyone else scenario is what makes this game so much fun. I've played a bunch of times, and only once has the betrayer been victorious (and that happened to be when I was the betrayer). Great game all around. It's...

This is my favorite game of all. The beginning game is simple enough to get everyone up to speed and feeling comfortable with the mechanics. Then one of you will betray the others, as determined by the system. Each side has hidden win conditions. This game is full of emergent story (I personally enjoy the games where the 8 year old girl turns traitor and wi...

This is, by far, Avalon Hill's best non-warfare game. This was the peak of their game development. Unfortunately, that means that after this game, their ideas went downhill from there. In this game, you play as a character, exploring a haunted house, looking for clues and items. The house is built from randomly shuffled tiles, so the house is NEVER THE SAME...

Instead of diseases and outbreaks, the island is getting flooded and perhaps disappearing. Players/Explorers race to collect 4 treasures and fly away. Things that make it sim...

Seven plays in with 2, 3 and 4 players each played at least twice. Jogo indicado para Team Building, por ser cooperativo e do género em que todos ganham, ou todos perdem.
