Nice family coop game. Components are very good en the game has a very tense feel to it. Not sure how much good play is rewarded as most of the choices seemed pretty obvious. But one should not forget it is aimed at different age group than Pandemic. So all in all a solid family game. Gameplay: :star::star::star::halfstar::nostar: Replayability: :star::star...

Fun little boardgame that can be enjoyed way below the recommended age range. My 5 year old son picked up the mchanics of this game after only 1 play and seems to enjoy it (he has asked to play it again). The only change I made to the mechanics was to remove the hand size limit of 5 cards. It's not that large of a change in my opinion, and I think it helped...

positive.text: Short, challenging game that requires strategy and cooperation to win. Some luck and chaos too. Theme is rich. Bits are first class. Very cheap price. Tons of fun. Playing time is about 30 minutes. For me, it definitely has that "Let's play again!" aspect. About as complex as Pandemic overall but a little shorter. Besides their different themes, a key diffe...

Just picked up a copy to play with my children. They like Pandemic but some of the strategy is beyond them. I hope this is a better fit for them. Edit -- This game is an absolute blast and has become my daughter's favorite. Highly recommended as a family/non-gamer game. Edit -- Rated as a family game.

Simple rules, fast-paced play, and beautiful artwork on the "board" combine to make this a favorite of ours. Given how simple it is, there's a lot variation from one game to the next due to the different initial set-up of the island and the different player roles. We've found that it gets distinctly harder with fewer players, as the limited number of treasu...

It's true, I definitely enjoy Pandemic much more for the added nuance (i.e., complexity). But Forbidden Island is great for playing with mixed groups or with kids. Games that work well for adults and kids playing together are actually extremely rare, and good ones are rarer still. True "gateway" games that can really engage both hobbyists and non-hobbyists...

Took a few plays to get past the comparison to Pandemic which we absolutely love. Now it is our number one gateway game that plays fast and we can still enjoy it with noobs. Has plenty to talk about. Fortunately there is something about this co-op that gets noobs contributing sound ideas and we don't find the experienced players completly dominating.

critical.text: My review here: For some reason I just have no desire to play LoW after my first 6 or so games. Still, as a low difficulty WP game with nice components, it has a spot in my collection. I just wish the box was more of a standard size. Sold at BGG.CON 2012 for $30 via virtual flea market.

Another worker placement game with a D&D theme pasted on. After a few plays the D&D charm wears off and it boils down to placing workers and resource collection. You know you've reached that point when people start referring to the adventurers as orange cubes instead of fighters, purple cubes instead of wizards.

I was initially really excited about this game. The production is good, I like the art, the rules seem straight forward and fun. The problem is that there is nothing special about this game, the mechanics all work but they all work better in other games. I don't feel drawn to playing it there aren't enough novel decisions or unique elements to encourage the...

I don't like take-that which can be targeted at a specific player versus the whole table. Sure, it is a viable design choice used to rein in the leader(s) but too often it gets employed as tit-for-tat as opposed to targeted for optimal play and that never fails to depress me. Of course, a devil's advocate would point out this is a problem with the players,...

Sometimes, the theme of a game can carry it, even if the mechanics don't leave lots of room for strategy. D&D itself is perhaps the poster child for this kind of game, to the point that you don't win or lose, you just tell a story. So a D&D-themed worker placement game seems like it could really integrate a lot of theme into what is sometimes a dry genre of...

mixed.text: Thank you Secret Santa 2018 ! Played this once and loved the feeling while playing it. The game itself is not that deep (How much more Euro than collecting and spending tiny cubes of colour) - but the theme seems to bring it to life. The various options available on the board for the most part felt like they would all give you some real benefit but there wa...

Добротное евро. Ничего сверхвосторженного. Нравится Кайлюс - понравится и эта. Сеттинг - сугубо наносное, визарды выжимают капельки из брендовой собственности. Общий дизайн и компоненты хорошие. Дизайн карт порадовал - пользоваться удобно. Концепция англ. рулбука на четверочку. Русский перевод Носова добавляет несуразностей и ляпов.

A real surprise for me! A quick resource collection / worker placement game with a little bit of Caylus (build buildings which create additional actions and provide benefits to the builder when others use them) and a little bit of Ticket To Ride (collect specific types of resources to finish quests. It's light, fun, and interactive.

Rating is for the Ios implementation. I've played it 4 times now. the tutorial is good. Interface is excellent. when I mix the AI strengths the highest AI was never the hardest opponent. When the AI strength is the same the medium AI allready offers me a challenge. the hidden roles, but certainly the quests and the buildings that come up make sure that ever...

- Great gateway game. - Simple rules and symbology. - Easy to teach/learn and fun to play. - I wouldn't play it without the skullport expansion as corruption adds intrigue, interaction and push your luck to the game. - I wish it didn't say Dungeons and Dragons on it, as this turns non-gamers off, despite it having nothing to do with the gameplay. - I also w...

positive.text: Pushed this one to a 10. I consider this my favorite worker placement game, and I play it on my iPad on a regular basis since it doesn't get a chance to get to the table very often. Which is fine, because I like it either way. The expansion improves the base game tremendously. I have also "pimped" my copy to the near-max by obtaining the various items from...

VERY fun game! I realize it is a D&D themed cube-pusher, but I LOVE THAT! I love the added segregation and luck-of-the-draw elements of the Quest deck. I like the limited availability of the buildings and the escalating VP accumulation on those available for build. I even like that some of the Intrigue cards are MUCH better than others. It all boils down to...

Fantastic game! Euro-style worker placement with plenty of twists and replay-ability. Excellent box design, components are of good quality, with good story and consistent theme. The game is fun for all. Last place still wins, as it is time well spent having fun with friends. Not a cut-throat game, very few direct attacks, though as it is resource placement...

Lords of Waterdeep is a simple game, yet is very rich and fulfilling. Both new and experienced gamers typically enjoy it, even at the same table. It is a superb gateway game, and many fans have this featured on their family game night. I actually know of one family that has 3 generations playing it together. This game will have a presence in the gaming indu...

I am revising my rating of this game to a '10' after about a dozen plays. I currently have over 200 games and as of this time, this game is my only '10'. This game is fun, easy to teach, and plays in an hour. Standard mechanics similar to Agricola or Stone Age, but in a bit simpler presentation. The Intrigue cards offer a chance to mess with opponents by ta...

critical.text: An adventure style game which, for me, tends to drag on far too long. I would prefer to get in 2-3 other games in the time it takes to set up and execute this one. Recent edition puts too much information cards, I miss the feel of the old booklet and another player reading what happened. After the first read through the actions at the site cards, it turns i...

This game would be great if it was at least somewhat challenging. But if you have even a clue of what to do, it is DIFFICULT to lose, because the old one just cant enter play. I like the theme and all, but whats the point of playing a cooperative game that you cant lose? Funrthermore, many times, the game reaches a point where the outcome is nearly certain,...

I wanted to like this one. It has nice and lots (poss too many) pieces/cards but there is too much downtime for my liking. And then when you do get a go it can be over in an unexciting second. I like the idea but don't think it is the best co-op game. It also seemed to be very easy to win. I do like some of the mechanics, so could be persuaded to play again.

Just received, but no play yet. The components overall are stunning, both in appearance and physical quality. I think the board in the original game was cheesier, but better looking -- this one is rather dark. Regardless of how the game plays, this one might be irresistible for the Lovecraft fans (like me!). Anyway, for less than $35 from Boulder Games, I d...

This is not so much a game as an unfolding story and you, the viewer/player, get to insert some decisions on which way to go and less often about what to do. Possibly the single most important thing you can do on each turn is to tweak your character abilities before moving to an encounter spot. At four hours per play, there is too much chrome and not enough...

mixed.text: Un juego de aventuras muy bien conseguido basado en los mitos de Cthulhu, sobretodo por la ambientación que se logra por medio de las cartas. Tiene una dificultad muy ajustada. a 3,4,5 jugadores si no se hace o muy difícil ganr o entre turnos larguísimos. Grandísimos componentes. Lo peor del juego el montarlo y guardarlo.

Great theme, graphic content, design and excellent mechanics. How I love this game. More cards than casino stockroom, but this is the game I enjoy showing to non-gamers as an expression of good game design. This game would be worth a 10 in my books, but game length tends to limit is playability and that must mark it down against more accessible and shorter...

Fantastic game idea with a wonderful theme. The game is a little unbalanced (OK, maybe more than a little!), but the core of the game is so cool, that fans of the game have devised all sorts of variants to make things more interesting. The game takes way too long to play, but it is still amazing. I would give it a perfect 10 if someone could devise a balanc...

Can take a while to set up and finish a game, but once you get going it's really good. And it can be played solo. I sometimes have a game on the table and work my way through a four-investigator game over the course of a week. So far I haven't finished before the cat found the table, but it is still great fun.

The game has some faults, some strengths, too much to describe in a short text. The one thing that really elevates this game is the atmosphere it creates and the interaction between players; irregardless of new or experienced players with this system, its always a bucket of laughs, creative comments, and you never really feel the down-time.

positive.text: Raised rating to a 10, because it's one game I still really look forward to playing, after having done so many, many times. In my opinion, this is the perfect style of game--just enough randomness to make each game exciting and unique. I don't remember what happened any of the times I played Puerto Rico, but a game of Arkham Horror can stick with me for wee...

Looooooooooong. Played with 7 players... lots of down time and got mind-numbingly dull. However, I will play again - with a smaller group and see if this one cant get redeemed. Can so many BGG'ers be wrong?? UPDATE: 04-25-09 Played it with the CVW again last night after a long hiatus. I was pretty solid on the rules, but there is still a lot going on here a...

This game just plain rocks. It has a very strong theme and story going for it and transports the lovecraftian Mythos very well. The co-operative nature works like a charm as players have to work hard to try and beat the game. It's hard to win, but it's lots of fun even when you lose. And the stories you get to experience are sometimes odd, sometimes fun, an...

This game is NASTY! My friends and I have played 4-5 times and we've only beat it once! And in spite of that, it is extremely fun. Update: The last couple of times we've played this, we beat it both times. They were in a 2 player situation both times and we went with a house rule that when you are knocked out or go insane you only lose 1 item or spell inste...

I'm eating crow on this one, I initially thought this was an good game buyoed primarily by the Lovecraft theme but after 10 plays I think this game is tremendous in terms of an old fashioned, 1980s style adventure game. Arkham Horror is clearly the best of that field chiefly due to the ridiculous number of interactions, possibilities, and variety the game o...

critical.text: I honestly don't know what all the hoopla is about with this game. It is a simple worker placement game that draws liberally (and blatantly) from previous games like Pillars of the Earth and Caylus. I would much rather play Pillars, which has more going on without the brain-burning of Caylus. There is nothing wrong with Stone Age, but it sure doesn't feel l...

Its good to have a dice game where I feel like I'm controlling the dice rather than the dice controlling me. An easy game to learn with superb pieces and board. This has plenty of depth. Edit - Just not enjoying it as much now. The blend doesn't work for me. I'd rather be playing Kingsburg, and have some intersting decisions to make.

Another worker placement game in the vein of PotE, ItSotE and Caylus but with two new and neat twists: 1. Varied order of actions after selection versus ordered or immediate 2. Dice rolling for food and resources. It was light, encouraged table talk and played in about 2 hours. All great features. I would like to try the 4 player version as I think it would...

If you've played other worker placement games and disliked the fact that you can count on what resources you'll come away with, then this game is for you. Two players putting the same number of workers on the same spot can walk away with pretty different outcomes for resources. Since these resources turn in to points, there's a whole game that has the final...

Players try to work their tribe of stone age cave peoples, and gain victory points. Another game where pawns are placed, resources gathered, and ultimately traded for victory points. Almost entirely lifted from other games we've seen in the past three years. The good thing is it all works, is made in Europe (quality bits), and looks stunning. The bad thing...

mixed.text: Stone Age is one of the all-time great gateway games, and a terrific introduction to worker placement. I didn't buy it for ages because it is a lighter game, but I realized that I always come back to talking about it when discussing games with people. Decided it needed to be on my shelf and I can't wait to try it out on newer gamers!

Cool little game, really awesome game board I love the whole stone age theme. it is one of the most beautiful games I have seen. I love the worker placement, love the dice mech, as with any reasource they are not constiant in the real world. great fun and appeals to many diffrent people.

6/13/13 Game Night - One game in and I crushed it! 6/15-16/13 Played with GF this weekend and she liked it. Very little downtime in a 2 player game, which is just why I thought it would be a good one for us. Played many games of this. Tragically it was the game being played on the fateful "Night the table got flipped."

I hate games where dice control your resources. The game is actually a lot of fun outside of the rolling dice part. I just wish there was a better way to get resources. This isn't a problem in Settlers because of the trading component. I understand why trading isn't implemented in this game as well, but still it's a bit frustrating that you're at the will o...

I may need to upgrade or downgrade this with future plays. You have a tribe of meeples, who you allocate to gathering various sorts or resources. You can build farms, or gather food to feed them, you can make tools (or more meeples), or you can get wood, clay, stone, or gold, to convert into victory points (which come in two flavours). It has dice but feels...

positive.text: I played this four times at the 2008 Gathering of Friends and purchased it the same week (which says something, since I purchase games very selectively these days). I found Stone Age to be quite engaging. I tend to rank games that really grab me a bit low with the intention of bumping up the rating if the title stands up to the test of time. I think Stone A...

Have played 5 games now, 2P and 3P with kids, (8 & 12). Kids picked it up quickly and my 12 yr old LOVES to play it. 2P games ran less than an hour, the 3P, just over. Don't see a problem with resources running out, that would be a hoarding problem. Good quality, pretty game. I'll play it whenever, who will set it up? 11/08 ****01/2011***okay, had to bump t...

This game packs alot of fun within 60 minutes! I love the combination of set-collecting, dice rolling and worker placement. It's also easy to teach to non-gamers. Every non-gamer I've introduced this to says that it's fun and not too difficult to play - that's a big thumbs up I'd say!

Lovely resource-management / worker-placement game. Simple enough to appeal to non-gamers, but still has the edge that makes it fun. Probably better on BSW, as the actual game is quite fiddly. Think I became too good at it, but now that I haven't played in a while, I am back with the pack.

This game is a clear 10 for me in its online BSW format (and I don't make this statement lightly - check my ratings). In person I would give it a 9 or 8 because it is a bit too slow for frequent in person play. At half an hour the game is the best yet created (for my taste) - at 90 minutes it is also good but there are many games I would choose first. Since...

critical.text: This game is pretty neat the first few times one plays, but I find the replay value to be a bit lacking. Also, one notices a "gang up on the leader" effect that can slow the game to a crawl, and make it drag on for well over the listed hour play time. We have had games of this go for as long as 2 1/2 hours (with five people.)

It helps to enjoy this if you are or ever were into RPG's, otherwise the humor may be lost. I find this a fun, light game. WHatever strategy you have can be thwarted by the other players if they have the right cards. After a few plays through the jokes can get old and the game looses some appeal, but that's what the expansions are for!

Hilarious game... once or twice. Mostly a "Screw the leader" dicefest kind of game. If someone starts to win, everyone gangs up on him. As a result, the game-- drags-- too-- long. Playing time 45 minutes? Yeah, right. The two games I played lasted 1.5 to 2.5 hours. The cards are very funny to read through, but not funny enough to mask the broken and un-fun...

It was really fun and exciting for the first five games or so but after that I knew all the cards and the jokes and there wasn't much left in the game. If you're Dungeons & Dragons fan it's recommended that you play this at least once at some point because it really is fun for the first couple of games. (It's also way too expensive to be a card game, but I...

The game is hilarious for the first few games but once you know all the cards it can get quite boring. Looking at people playing the game for the first time is a blast too, though. If you want to have the game exciting for yourself too, prepare to buy lots and lots of add-ons (because there are lots and lots of 'em!).

mixed.text: It's Munchkin, some people hate it, some people love it. I'm one of the later... Or so I was... I guess I'm in the middle now... I still think it's a great game for the right kind of people. I used to be one of these, but I'm not anymore. I say that but I'm probably dusting it off tomorrow as I type this but it has literally been years since it's been playe...

First time I played this there were only two of us (we had just bought it and wanted to check it out before taking it to a friend's) and it was not much fun for two ppl. The second time (3 ppl) we ended up with a very weird deck where all the monsters were in the bottom and we managed to equip ourselves very well. Not much fun then either. But the other day...

I particularly enjoy this game, but only with the right people. The rules are vague on purpose and it is meant to instigate fighting over how to play. So while I would never try to get my family to play this with me, every time I have played it with friends we have always had a blast.

A fave among all my non-gamer friends!!! What gets most people, especially those who don't like games, is the very cute and smart cards, drawings, etc. It is over-priced but it is the only game I managed to find that serious gamers and non-gamers are always willing to play! Also makes a great gift.

I haven't logged all the games of Munchkin I've played, but we've played it A LOT. Most were played together with Unnatural Axe and Clerical Errors, and recently the Steeds were added. Even more recent, Rangers (Deranged Expansion) have also come into play... God these decks have become HUGE! And what about an extra deck... We now also play in the demented...

positive.text: This is one of my all time favorite games. Those who complain about it are just sore losers and were on the losing end of the gang-up. The rules even encourage this and make no effort to hide that fact. There are cards in the game that force you to help others and can give you immunity from attacks so there shouldn't be any complaints. Definitely a game for...

An excellent game altogether, as long as your players get into the spirit of it. Once people can see that they can be as merciless as possible, then the shouting and bickering and just plain fun begins :) If your group takes to it, add the expansions quickly or else it gets boring seeing the same cards.

Excellent card game for several people. The more RPG-ish are players, the more fun - if you don't know from experience how to "manage" MG you can miss a joke... Sometimes there is no time (or mood) to play but even browsing cards and reading the descriptions of monsters and "bad staff" that can happen to you makes a good laugh.

The original! This is one of our favorite games to play. So far we've picked up every card expansion (still missing some promos and 'extras') and we love it! Gameplay is fast and fun. Players can team up for or against one another and often, in our games, the person who is currently in the lead will get ganged up on to prevent them from winning. The only is...

While this game is highly based on luck, I know of few other games that can get cause the level of laughter and entertainment as Munchkin. I would suggest this game should be played with a minimum of 5 players (although you will need to own at least one expansion for this to work out well) as the lower the number of players, the more personal people seem to...

critical.text: I rate this game the same way I would rate Crack. It might be fun for a while but boy are you going to regret it. No matter how much you spend on this game, eventually you collection will seem wimply because the newer cards always get more powerful. Don't walk away, run. (In my gaming group we call Magic "flat crack")

At heart, this is a great game. Unfortunately, it was wrecked by years and years of bad designed cards (caused by an excessive quantity of expansions). Nonetheless, I enjoy playing it in "limited" formats nowadays. Lack (or excess) of mana can ruin any game, though. This would probably not happen if this game was from 2003 instead of 1993...

I have (had) far too much M:tG stuff. I never play anymore and I will never buy another card. There are so many better games out there that cost so much less. I could have given this a [1], being responsible for the awful capitalist CCG craze (particularly Pokemon, preying on children with susceptible parents). On the other hand, the game is actually quite...

No surprise to anyone that I loved this game when it came out. I grew disillusioned after about a year. Every other game was a blowout due to drawing too much or too little land, a flaw inherent in the game that can't be fixed by any card design. Shadowfist was clearly an improvement on many of the same CCG principles.

mixed.text: This one is hard and weird to rate as I've spent more time with MTG than any other game, not even close. I would love to play it - which is how I rate - but wouldn't want to be in that world anymore. And if I would own it I know that I would gravitate towards the center of the black hole... so I don't own it, won't play it.... but still rate it a 9.... weir...

Magic the Gathering is one of my all-time favorite games. I spent years playing, collecting and trading MTG cards, and I loved every minute of it. My only disgruntlement with this game (and other similar card games) is the requirement of constantly shelling out money for expensive cards, as I've grown up into Mr. Frugal and don't like spending lots of money...

This is an amazing game with tons of support and formats. One of the best TCGP (if not THE best) out there... but it also is VERY expensive and takes a lot to get into. If you are into TCGP there is no better... but it is still not something I would recommend to all and think you might be better served getting a bunch of board games for a cheaper cost. Stil...

Fast playing game, but one in three games is a dud due to lack of lands required for reasonably playability (or occasionally a land flood). Lots of variety, but at a high price compared to many good quality games (such as Race for the Galaxy in particular) - Magic is definitely not good value for money. I love the sealed deck tournaments, though!

I will always remember my great experiences with this game. It changed my gaming culture, so to speak. It opened my eyes to the evolving gaming market. There was NOTHING like opening up a pack of The Dark, and hoping to get the Maze of Ith! lol! Would rate higher if not for the monopoly Wizards puts on this genre. Other fine games cannot survive because of...

positive.text: Earlier: Good game strangled under expensive card-collecting. A lifestyle game that is overly complicated for my current life. 2018: My son got interested, we started with some preconstructed decks, then got kiloboxes, and since then I've bought random assortments of cards from people who've stopped playing. I now have thousands of cards. Oops. But Magic is...

Fabulous CCG that started the frenzy. Very well done card art and elegant gameplay, although the rules have become so complex that WOTC began printing specific rules instructions for special abilities right on the cards. Technically only meant for two players, multiplayer rules are easy to come by.

Just being the original CCG game gives this game huge bonus points. Everyone else who came after could work off the basics of this game, but for the first go round at this sort of thing, they did a fantastic job. The only downside of the game is the cost involved and the rules can get tricky with some cards causing problems with others. If you just booster...

Magic: The Addiction is an amazing, absorbing, consuming game with the power to take over your life. It has so many possible combinations, and there is tremendous strategy to both building decks and playing the game. Downside is the heavy time and financial committment involved in a collectible card game.

Incredible game botched by inept marketing and production by Wizards of the Coast and Hasbro. While enjoyable to play, the continuous production of expansion sets and revisement of tournament rules makes organized play impossible for anyone with financial concerns (read: most everyone). I play casual sealed deck with my wife sometimes even now; it is truly...

I don't think there is all that much replayability or many different strategies in this one. Bit disappointed actually :soblue: Sold in 2017.

Un juego extremadamente simple que se agota a las 2 partidas. Para jugar con niños puede tener cierto sentido, aunque creo que hay opciones mejores. El juego consiste únicamente en un pequeño puzzle vitaminado. Con adultos la diversión desaparece casi antes de aparecer. Se le busca otro hogar y ya está.

good little 2p game with 2 kinds of "time track" mechanic I like [+] the whole track of tile offers some very interesting choices (how much am I willing to pay, what am I giving up on the way, what possibilities am I opening for my oponent), the milestones (scoring, bonus) on the time track offer a second level of objectives, I like the spatial puzzle eleme...

critical.text: Unremarkable 2 player filler. It's light, it's pretty quick to explain - but luck is a significant factor in game play, if you get a run of high value goods you'll do well. Overall felt pretty underwhelmed playing it - nothing obviously wrong, just not much fun. Many other quick 2 player games I'd rather play.

Meh. I wanted to like Jaipur as I find its colors pretty and I'd like more good two player games. Unfortunately it isn't very memorable. It's not that it's bad but it's not really good either. It's hard to fine tune your strategy as there is too much randomness in the scoring points so you end up playing conservatively most of the time, merely trying to avo...

This looked promising based on the BGG reviews, but it turns out it's VERY light with mostly obvious decisions. The game kind of plays itself once you learn the basic tactics - which takes one game at the most. For a short and simple two-player card game, I'd much rather play Schotten Totten (Battle Line), Lost Cities, Kupferkessel Co, or several others.

After just one round, my sister said, "A little fiddly, and not enough oomph." She's right. Jaipur is beautifully produced, right down to the vivid artwork and sculpted box insert. But sorting and stacking the 50+ beautiful bonus disks is a bummer before each round. That would be fine if the game were substantial, but it's a fluffy "best of three" affair wi...

2013-06-24 Initial Rating: 7.0 (August 2012) Initially I really liked this game, nowadays I have cooled a little toward it. This is a good family game, with simple rules but with some interesting/hard decisions, still it is a bit light for my taste. The game flows rather quickly and my GF loves it so I don’t think I will sell it. The theme is paper thin for...

mixed.text: A fun and quick little two-player trading game with cards that works better than you think it would. There is quite a bit of depth to this game and the set collection for some reason reminds me of Splendor, even though it really isn't. Great presentation and an excellent game to take on travels!

Wow, I can't believe how much I enjoy this simple little card game. To me it's an improvement on Splendor; though different, it has a similar feel (and both games are currently tussling with one another on the BGG rankings). As set collection goes this does it best. When to collect, when to sell, when to flood the market with camels - and the art and theme...

Emma cajoled me into trying this during the last 20 minutes of our attendance at UKGE2024 as she saw it layed out on a demo table and liked how it looked. I was worn out and my enthusiasm was low. Boy am I glad she suggested it. We were taught really well by the demo guy and the game is super fun. Lots of decisions and gameplay packed into a tight little ch...

Quick set collecting game that's good fun for two-players The camel cards and tight hand limit really make the game worth quick plays here n there Glad I own it - this is one I even play online at Board Game Arena ------------- Played with a knowledgeable player and the games were back n forth with a lot more strategy then one would think possible - what a...

Game is nice. We really love trading and market type games. Jaipur sounded like we bohnanzalovers would like it, and we do. But it is a bit fiddly, to set up takes a while and the fact that this game is 'best of three' you have to set it up three times per game. Counting scores can be a bit time consuming as well.... Last thing, the market is very luck base...

positive.text: Played 15-20 times since 2011. If you are looking for a quick, simple, interesting two-player game, you can´t go wrong with Jaipur. One of my very few 10s. Each round takes about 15 minutes, so 30 or 45 minutes in total. The amount of luck is just right for a game like this, I think, though I´m sure the variable points on bonus tokens can bother some player...

Jaipur is a light hand management game that is a delight to play. It is not a brain burner by any means, but it is very fun and fast. You can make some clever moves with your timing of camel use but the randomness of card draws is a heavy decider in the winner. Fun Factor : :star::star::star::star::star: Fulfillment Factor : :star::star::star::nostar::nosta...

Delightful and Excellent 2 Player Set Collection, Trading-Themed, Hand Management Card Game !! Games can be quick. This one really grew on me. The games get brutal with seasoned players. This is probably our goto quick 2-player card game. I finally won a game with my wife after a few years. It's so fun, fast, and furious with us.

positive.text: This is everything I want from a co-op. Enough complexity to ward off one person from taking over the game, and also enough to keep each player's interest. I've watched this game be refined over time, and it's been slowly polished into a gem. Should be one of the top hits of 2017.

The beginner game sacrifices no core play at all. In fact, it allows new players to play the beginner game while others play "normally". It's a model for how any beginner play should work in more complex game...

positive.text: A true classic. Many gamers hate this game because its so old and doesn't play like a "modern game." Hello? You need to invent the wheel first before you can improve upon it. Say what you will, you German Game elitists, but this is STILL one of the best games ever! There's nothing quite so satisfying as collecting rent for a Hotel on the Orange properties or for several houses on the Greens from the unlucky soul who lands there, whether it's your best friend or Mom or your know-it-all teenage son!

The heart of this game is the trading and negotiating. If you enjoy this aspect of gameplaying, there are only a few other games which match the enjoyment of this one. As with all games that depend on a lot of player interaction, a session will live or die based on who you're playing with.

This is one of my all time favorite games. Maybe it is nostalgia, or maybe because I generally win. I always have fun playing this game and I am always willing to drag it out for a quick game. The rest of my Monopoly boards I will rate on how I like the board not the game itself.

Monopoly is criminally underrated on BGG. It reminds me a bit of the way music snobs used to talk about pop music before poptimism became a thing. If I don't win I feel bad because I will no doubt have done something dumb. If I win I feel bad for my opponent who most likely did something dumb. At this moment in time I really don't like chess thus the low rating. Feb 04 *...

I appreciate the strength of chess but rarely have the urge to improve my game through study, which leaves me in limbo play-wise. I generally play this against a computer opponent, so I can fine tune the AI for a 'sweet spot' challenge. Despite this, it's not often that I feel like a game.

Unfortunately I find chess has been so thoroughly analysed it has for many become a game of who can memorise the furthest into a strong opening sequence. In any event, while fairly elegant, chess can be quite dry. The problem with any game where the better player almost always wins is, well, why play? To see who's better at a game? Hmmm.

I used to enjoy collecting inexpensive chess sets. Both my interest and number of sets have since decayed, much to my chagrin. In more recent years, I've found that 'standard' chess bores me to tears, and I'll avoid playing it as long as there is something else to play. Despite this, I still consider chess to be a good game, but it just doesn't appeal to me...

This is a perfect example of a great game, which is why a lot of people don't play it. It has absolutely no luck mechanics, requires deep look-ahead, and doesn't have comeback mechanics. When i want a brain burner this is served up. Classic and respected game in the western world however I now realize that there is so much more out there. There are many aspects of chess that I dont like: no talking, very tense, brutal, one player must crush the other, painful to play when you are behind. However it has been the best game for much of my life...

Hard to rate this. I prefer season 0 over season 1. Season 1 had too many characters to choose from. However season 0 is harder to internalize the rules for and avoid mistakes. I suspect I prefer season 0 over season 1 also because I've played pandemic so often the theme changes for season 0 are nice. Ranking this a 7.6 to reflect my belief that pandemic le...

If you like pandemic then this is a no brainer. For myself, liking pandemic but not wanting to play it that often due to the fact that no matter how well you play, if the cards come out in a bad order then (without knowing it) you've lost before the game even starts. The legacy system doesn't change this, it just helps mitigate being unlucky/lucky multiple...

This game is really difficult to rate. The novelty of the concept make it really enjoyable and based on that alone I would probably rate it a 9 or a 9.5. But we had the problem that the 2-Player game was way too easy (even with all the epidemic cards) and we just breezed through the last three or four months. Coming to Legacy, I was a bit worried that the surprises for veteran players would be minimal. That I'd enjoy...

Pandemic is a favorite so I was already set up to love this. The changing elements in each game, narrative arc, and evolving objectives really work well here in creating a super compelling reason to just keep playing. It's also been a ton of fun to play with the same group for each game - time with friends is what this hobby is all about. This certainly des...

5 plays in and we're in April. I had high expectations going in to this game and thus far it has not disappointed. The only real mark against it is that you should try to play...

The resulting experience continuously shifts just enough that the individual rounds...

Wow, just 2 plays in (both losses) and we've had a great time. The few subtle changes that they've made so far are great. After playing through March we've added so many new things. But whenever you claim to have a card, other players can challenge your claim. Or claim to have the card that defends them. Nice game, and plays up to six. But in my games, bluffing didn't seem to happen...

This is a really quick and simply card game composed of only 15 cards. There are 5 cards with 3 copies of each. The game is played with each player taking a turn until only one person has survived. Each player will be dealt 2 cards which will be placed facedown after being looked at by their respective player. Your facedown cards are your hit points. On you...

A game of role deduction and bluffing that definitely surpasses Werewolf, The Resistance, and the like. It's carefully designed and super short. Reminds me a little of Love Letter minus the card play, sort of. Fits that same niche. Benefits from experienced tables that know how and when to lie about their roles.

Love the idea of this. Quick playing, deduction + bluffing, etc. The stakes are a little high, which is fine if it stays quick, but playing with slower players raises the consequences of being wrong which lowers the bluffing and bluff calling which makes the game longer, so it can easily spiral into stalemates. When this happens, it all comes down to who ha...

mixed.text: The simplicity and elegance of the game is stunning. The fact that you can ''play'' any role by pretending to have the card is great. There's a lot of bluff and a lot of deduction involved, which makes the game similar to poker in some ways. Unfortunately, when you're down to 3 players or so, there's a very strong kingmaker aspect to the game that makes it...

Very basic game, but the simplicity is what makes it easy to form strategies and not feel like luck has such a large impact on the gameplay. Just try not to play it too much with the same group of people since people since people will slowly default to the same strategies and it'll start to get repetitive very quickly.

Fun social deduction game that plays in less than 10 min per round. Everyone has a role that allows them to do an action against or in defense of anyone else. But you can also just lie and say that you have a role, that is until someone calls you out on it! Mix between the older card game "BS" and games like resistance/werewolf. Dead simple to learn, play s...

I wish my recorded plays actually reflected the number of times I've played this game. A session of coup is usually like 15 plays back to back. This is great fun to play with a small group of friends of love bluffing, and stabbing each other in the back. Fantastic filler for the main attractions on game night.

Coup is simple and fun, a bluffing game that doesn't require a lot of skill to play but much more so if you want to become a bluffing master. It is very enjoyable with 5 people and takes only 15 minutes to play; lack of variety in the cards can cause a group to play a couple of rounds and then pack it away, its simplicity making it only so much fun in one s...

positive.text: Players represent Italian families during the Renaissance, wielding power and influence. There are 15 cards in the game, 3 each of the Duke, Captain, Contessa, Assassin and Ambassador. These five types of cards each grant a special power in the game. Two of these cards are dealt to each player, face down, and are ideally kept hidden throughout the game. On...

Simple and brilliant - had tons of fun with it with both hardcore gamers and casual gamers. Really easy to pick up, super quick and by the third game you can be knee deep into your lying. The art in this kickstarter version is superb - and kodus to having an inclusive and diverse set of characters, a rarity in gaming.

Light games consisting of a small deck of cards and hidden roles are in right now. Coup is the best one. Equal parts deduction, calculation, and deception, Coup forces you try and survive five tense minutes in which players use the powers of face down character cards to accumulate resources and eliminate other players. I have been telling people this is the best game design I have ever seen. I have gone very deep with this game, not quite charting out endgames and all that, but playing hundreds of rounds over the years. It is a polished jewel. In this game, you only have one or two hole cards, but you can make a move represented by any of the five hole cards, as long as n...

There are some games that are long and complicated. And glorious. You play them a few times, trying out a few strategies, eventually internalising the rules, then you move on to the next one. Then there is Coup. Minimal rules, can be played a half dozen times in a session. And it is glorious. We play Coup lots. I don't know much about your Coup. I know more...

critical.text: Will still play occasionally. Fun and flawed. I'll play Machiavelli over an entire weekend, but Risk gets dull after an hour -- and it can last six hours. Huge endgame problem -- good players can hold out forever. Mission cards and hidden capitols help a bit. On the other hand, the rules are simple, and with the right players it can be fluid.

This is a classic. Maybe the grand-daddy of wargamming. No it's not Go or Chess or Diplomacy but it deserves betters than a lousy 6. For many a wargamer this was first and we are "Geeks" in some way due to this game. Looking back when compared with German games and some of the better games from NAm designers this game looses some points but come on it's a f...

Why do some people go on and on about how Risk is brilliant? There is only one tactic to win (sit in one corner, preferably Australia or South America, until you have a big pile of re-inforcements and try to win in one go) and it's basicly all about luck. Very little skill or insight is required to play Risk, only play as a time filler with like-minded indi...

I feel like should give this a higher ranking but I can't - the world has just produced so many superior descendants and offshoots, there is no reason to play this anymore. Perhaps use this game to introduce your child to the genre, but understand that it is a dicefest and overly simplistic. Unlike some of the games of my childhood, I don't actively regret...

Get North America. If too difficult, aim for Africa, South America, or Australia. Only 2 defending points ocne you've eaten up the others within the territory. Also, too dependent on who will get the right cards and thus the bonus armies. With later additions, the secret independent goals added some to the game, instead of winning when taking the whole worl...

mixed.text: I have played this several times. Many of those, I can recall events that caused my victory or defeat. It is a classic and a good basic strategy game for beginners. The only draw back... it takes forever. My friends and I usually play it as a World Domination Night with several other games on hand for the players that get eliminated.

A lot better than most on BGG would admit to, there is a lot of luck involved, but there is still some strategy, not without its merits, a good thing to do is add your own mission cards and make capitals, if you lose your capital your out and your army becomes neutral, you can't change your capital etc.

Hey, it's Risk. I like this game. Once played against a guy who owned Australia and spent the entire game just depositing armies into Australia while the rest of the World battled it out. When it was time to take Australia, the rest of the World united in a common fear of the Aussie invasion. Then it was back to war as usual.

Risk is still great! If anyone asked me I'd be ready to play. Yes, I know there are many better games out there now -- but hey, any game that brings back memories from childhood, teenage and college years holds a special place in my heart. It's just the long, long games that are painful, especially when you are losing :)

Great way to introduce kids to boardgaming. Very simple mechanics, but it's the player interaction that makes this game shine. The classic "Sure you can leave that border undefended, I won't attack you next turn"-method of breaking alliances, friendships, and losing everything on the roll of a dice :)

positive.text: Ah yes! The one true game that started and coined the term "Beer & Pretzels" for all other war games that had a lot of rolling dice. But hey, you have to know when to attack, or when to just sit in Siam and build up your army totally, right? You have to know when to take that risk (no pun intended). This game will always be a huge favorite multi-player game...

I still love this game even after playing other more realistic war games. Risk should be honored for creating the war genre. A truly visionary game like Monopoly and Clue. I LOVE the updated Risk 2210, but I always will have a place in my heart and dice in my hands for classic Risk. Fun, Fun, Fun!!!

Learned in 1964, age 12, been a great fan ever since. Still have the copy I bought in college in 1970, that we played to death. It's a wonder we're all still friends! Best version is with wooden pieces -- nothing more intimidating than 50 blocks and a few beans in Kamchatka, attacking Alaska!

A classic, for sure! I played as a child with the old wooden cube armies (loved that shade of pink!) and play now with my children using the new basic version with plastic pieces. I like the addition of the army-shaped pieces, with different things representing different numbers. It's fun for my kids to change out their five foot soldiers to a soldier on a...

in the popular sport of Risk bashing, people forget some of the great things about Risk - you can follow many different strategies and none of them are victims to dice - i have never lost a game due to die rolling as you take this into account and mass your armies accordingly - the player interaction is top notch - lends it self to alliances, temporary and...

critical.text: Para mi Hanabi es el mejor juego de su autor Antoine Bauza. Un solitario colaborativo que cuenta con la deducción aparte del azar para intentar concluirlo con éxito. Un juego que resulta muy divertido por el grado de confusión que los jugadores pueden sufrir y el riesgo que hay que correr. Un juego muy de moda a finales de 2011 para terminar sesiones de jue...

Quite nice simple and fast cooperative game. I like it for its originality and for the way it solicits a different kind of cooperation between players. So I would have liked to give a higher rating, but, to be honest, I find the actual play a bit flat. There is no real tension, maybe because most of the time the team is just scoring an average score and so...

There were some aspects of this that were really fun, but it is a game that leads to recriminations afterwards - "Why did you tell me that/not play that" etc... Also, the fact that you don't win or lose really, but get a score for how well you did, somehow didn't work for me - even though you can say that 16 or more is a win really.

A cooperative deduction game. Have a 5 card suits - numbered 1-5 and are trying to play in order. The twist is that the player cannot see his own cards but only the ones the others have. You have to supply clues to the others of what to play or discard, you have a limited number of clues you can give before you must discard a card to get the ability to issu...

Benefits from card holders. Played with two and scored 19 on the second try and 25 on the fifth. Our other scores were pathetic (first 6 games). I get the impression that 2-player is more succeptible to luck of the shuffle than higher player counts. Update: Now we pretty much always score at least 23. Played one game with the multi-colored cards and scored...

mixed.text: Bought at Grand Con 9/27/2015 Played 9/28. Alicia and I got 19 points first play. I think she did better than I did. I missed some info by not paying enough attention to the "graveyard". White killed us as both 3s got discarded. Really enjoyed this one. Can't wait to see what happens with 4 or 5 players. Lovely and tactiley pleasing tiles. Stinky game box!

whilst co-operative games would not rank amongst my favourites, contrary to popular belief, I will play them -- and this is one of the best, easy, to play and yet so difficult to master and complete -- what clues are the best -- can your colleagues pick up on your intelligent hints (and especially vice versa) -- hopefully no one will stay angry at each othe...

Made our own deck. Had a great time playing a 5P game. We laughed and bonded over this game.....even though we had no idea what we were doing! :) Have played a few times as a 2P game which is also a fun way to play. Recommended game, but you need the right group/mind-set. At first we used no conventions....absolutely zero. Now we play with one convention: W...

I don't generally enjoy co-ops, but this one is different. The whole interesting aspect is the struggle not to convey information that you aren't permitted to. I know this is a part of many co-ops, but not to the same extent. We spent a while after the game rehashing what we were trying to convey.

Cleverly inverted co-op card game. The theme is a little thin (if a game with these mechanisms is going to have a pasted-on theme, I think it a better one would have been codebreaking or bank robbers trying to break into a safe). It's fun, fast, and easy to take with you. It's hard not to give away extra hints to other players through facial expressions, bu...

positive.text: Coop' petit format mais tellement malin que c'est un plaisir de le sortir. Le perfect a été atteint à 2 et 3 joueurs.... à quand pour la version 4 et 5 joueurs ? après plus de 100 parties, les techniques deviennent vraiment de plus en plus chiadé, c'est toujours un plaisir quand l'autre comprend la logique.

My wife and I REALLY enjoy this as a two player game. It takes practice with the same group of players to get good (assuming you don't allow cheating with your voice inflections). The only problem is that my wife and I are good enough with each other now (we only play with the rainbow cards anymore) that it can be frustrating to play with other people.

Probably the most amazing cooperative game ever. I have not played this original, but only the fan-made spinoff, but the basic principle is the same: You see everyone else's cards, but not your own, and the collective goal is to get out all cards in the right order. You can inform your teammate which of his card(s) are of a certain number or colour. This tu...

Christmas gift for Kim in 2013. Has become a favorite subsequently. Small cards games are usually big hits in our house. Played with or without positive/negative inflections and haven't seen a huge difference. Our record is 22 which was on our second play Christmas afternoon. Played with 2,3, and 4.

This is such an excellent game. It feels so different from any other game you'll play, which just feels so cool when you're playing it. It's quite difficult figuring out the best clues to give or how exactly to go about giving specific information when you're forced to give more general information than you'd like, all while trying to remember what everyone...

First impression: I had positive expectations but for some reason didn't like game. I lost both games by horrible mistakes but playing didn't feel fun at any point. Game itself is a brilliantly designed abstract that doesn't have board of any sort. About my love/hate relationship with abstracts, see my entry for Yinsh.

It features the same game play as Hive but with stylin' black-on-white and white-on-black pieces instead of the multicolor bugs running around in the current edition. Second Edition The components are among the highest tier in my collection and boost my rating way more than they should. I burned myself out on the Java applet of Hive a while back but have recently been reinvigorated by playing face to face (it's a whole different game). Hive is a more interesting and shorter version of Chess to me. It's compact, simple, y...

This is a great game to keep in your purse or in the glove compartment of your car for those unexpected waits. The game is eye-catchingly attractive and the rules are quite elegant. The game play scratches that hard to reach Chess itch without requiring book study to be competitive.

Although my husband beats me every time, I can't get enough of the enjoyable but basic strategy of trying to surround his queen bee with my ants, beetles, spiders and grasshoppers. Perfect game for travel too...we take this when we go camping or to play in hotels during overnight stays. Easy to learn, fun for pretty much any age or personality type. Plus, w...

Currently my most played game. Simply beautiful, with weighty, chunky Bakelite pieces. The depth of chess, but quicker, more fun, and more user friendly to beginners. FFS stop trying to fix the spider. It is not broken. Same goes for new players complaining about the white advantage. I've been playing for over ten years, and don't see it as an issue.

critical.text: A little conflicted on this one after playing half-a-dozen times. Is it good and entertaining? Sure. But somehow it doesn't rise to the level of being at all engrossing like some of the better light wargames (Wizard Kings, for instance). For me, I don't agonize over choices, decisions are generally pretty obvious. Sometimes the flavor is good and it feels l...

Note: I do not care for the Command and Colors system so my opinion is biased. I found this to be an improvement over Battle Cry but still lacking in feel. If I am going to play a wargame, it should offer the feel of massive armies. All of the C&C games are small scale tactical battles...something I have never cared for. It is a good game just one that I do...

Not sure what to make of this game, I can't rate it yet. It certainly has excellent components and is a very easy game to play. Reminds me of when I was 10 and crawled around on the floor playing battles with 1/72 scale soldiers...still just as bloody and random. I like the stance it has with youngsters and it is undoubtably a gaming dream for anyone under...

Decent for what it is. More of a kid or family game (if your family is really into WWII). Certainly overrated at the moment. Artillery figures are an abomination...others are good. Nice board and tiles. Scenario editor will be available on website, but charging $20 (or alternatively owning two copies) for full version is a joke. (What, I have to pay for the...

When I first got Memoir '44, I played it a bunch and really enjoyed it. The games were fast and exciting and had a sense of history about them. I was inspired to seek out more detailed war games like Twilight Struggle, Combat Commander and Warriors of God to name a few. Coming back to it after exploring the lighter end of the wargame genre I found Memoir '4...

mixed.text: I never think I'm going to enjoy playing this when it's brought out, but then I always do. It's quick, but not *too* quick, and it's tricky, but not *too* tricky. Not to mention educational, but not *too* educational. (: A nice, briskly-paced WWII game, attractively made and infinitely variable.

There are certainly better games--and I feel like I graduated from Memoir '44 to Combat Commander, finishing my degree in WWII Hand Management Studies--but few things can compare to the joy of pushing around my little plastic army men and rolling my little dice with grenades on them. Commands & Colours might be my favorite wargame system only for its having...

Entry level war-game with dice based combat. I've played multiple scenarios with my nephew to introduce war-game concepts. It's fun and plays quickly, although set up can take some time. Although the scenarios are actual historical battles, this is definitely not a simulation by any means.

A solid "war game." It's not truly a war game in the same space as World in Flames or any of the others you can find on here, but it is obviously a war game in simulation and theme. It's really fun, with several real world battles in the box that you can set up. I've enjoyed every game of this I've played and as a two player game it stands out as being a bi...

Ok! We were not sure about this game, as we really haven't gotten into war gaming at all! My wife tried wargaming with her father growing up, and said it just wasn't her thing! But...this game is incredible, after one game...the first scenario...she asked to play again...and again... So this was a great purchase, and we both finally feel that we do like war...

positive.text: I finally have the game and played it, and you bet I'm giving it a 10. There's just no other war game like it (well, except for BC). The simplicity stays in tact with quick reference cards that answers questions about the rules quickly. After all this talk, this game better make game of the year or something... after playing maybe 500+ games of BC, you can...

Great fun! Will see a lot of play. Repeated play leads to a desire to play more. Upgraded rating due to DoW customer service taking care of my issue with the figures, and because nongamers I know want to play it. Gameplay is fast and fun. The "as is" game is great, and this one will be a launching pad for a lot of fun house and optional rules...a delight fo...

Played a few times and love the game. Relatively simple and intuitive rules, lots of different scenarios (and scenery), nice web support/forums, and interesting, but not stiflingly involved strategy. Perhaps a bit too much luck is involved, as a match can sway heavily at the beginning depending on cards drawn. This tends to even out, I think, in the longer...

The more I play this game the better it gets! The card play and dice add such luck and randomness that even my 20+ years of playing war games does not guarantee a win against my wife who just started playing them! Fantastic game! If you have this one, you have to have the new Battle Cry game, too. Both are cast from the same mold, and are classics!

It's superb. I'm a big fan of Battle Cry, but Memoir '44 improves upon an already great thing. Days Of Wonder should be very proud. Also, I introduced it to my non-gaming wife and after the first game, I was thrilled to hear her ask if we could play again! Did you all catch that last comment??? Non-gamer wife... Played it... And LIKED it... ;-)

To be fair, this is purely unlucky, but I think being on the ropes from a cylon attack is half the fun of the game. When there are no cylons to fight, the game drags in...

critical.text: As far as pure auction games goes, this is one of the better ones if only because it strips the genre down to a minimialist level and doesn't try to couch the mechanic in another system or in an unrelated, nonsense theme. It's simple, quick, and easy to throw out and play with up to 6 which is good news to me. I don't think it deserves quite the status it s...

Ultra-light filler. High Society or Coloretto are much better at filling the niche of "the light yet interestimg game that gamers play between their main games". Best left for play with non-gamers and young kids. The first edition english rules are confusing, which is surprising for what should be a very simple game. The errata posted here on BGG is require...

Memory (of what cards have already been auctioned and played) is critical in this game. Strategy is important, but not nearly as important as memory, so it's not usually a very enjoyable game for me. But it's quick and easy -- 20-30 minutes max for a whole game, including teaching the game.

Components: The Überplay edition has nice money chips and checks, but the real estate images are the real winner, with a wonderful illustration for each of the 30 cards. The box is terribly oversized. Experience: Fast and mildly fun mixture of auction and blind bidding. Having a few cards removed (with fewer players) helps to keep the last few offerings in...

Got this as a quick to learn, quick to play game for my daughters (9 and 12) and me. Fits that bill supremely well as we can rattle off a game in 10 - 15 minutes. Actually, that is what I like most about this game -- the speed at which a complete start-to-finish can take place AND the game manages to do this with a cute story arc thrown in. It's like a game...

mixed.text: One of my absolute favorite fillers. It's like two games in one. Extremely quick playing, plenty of tough choices, multiple auction styles, intuitive to play, easy to explain and the art on the various properties is fun and suits the theme of the game perfectly. Very satisfying experience from such a quick game.

I probably rate fillers like this a bit too harshly. For Sale is really a smart, solid game. I'm happy to play it pretty much any time. There's a surprising amount of depth while still mantaining a light feel. Its perfect for new gamers and veterans looking for a quick way to pass the time.

This is an easy to learn filler that has two stages. The first stage is bidding on property and then the next stage is selling your properties. It's a good game and is a short filler game. I don't like it as much as No Thanks and Felicity the Cat in the Sack but it is still a good game.

positive.text: Simple and elegant. Quite possibly as good as Thor and tying in my book as the best filler card game. In fact, while it may not be a better game than Thor, I'd say that it beats it out in the "Fun" category. I've played both versions of For Sale and find that the Uberplay version works just fine. Beautiful art, nice price point, good job guys. UPDATE: Aw Cr...

A very quick "filler" bidding game in two phases, where first half is a progressive turn-based bidding/auction to acquire currency (checks) so that, in second phase, you use your checks for simultaneous bidding/auction to buy one realty from each community lot of house cards. It's crazy fun! but quick, light. The key trick lies in anticipating what your opp...

Fantastic filler game. This is the only game in my collection that has gotten immediate replay requests. Its first appearance at game night saw 7 playings! Can't recommend this one enough. *UPDATE 2/06* This game still holds a 10 rating for me. Its just such a beautiful, quick, tight game. Even the kids love it!

The King of all fillers. So simple, yet so brilliant... and you always want to play it again, right away. Okay, well I do. [rating for Uberplay version: 8. I miss the match-a-bid rule and the greater variance in the check cards. The system is still a winner, but the streamlining - they streamlined For Sale, fer Chrissakes! - may speed up gameplay (as if the...

Wow -- what a great little game! Not many better for the 10-15 minute filler category. I absolutely love the two phase approach, where you bid in the first half to "draft" cards you want to use to actually earn money in the second half. Incredibly clever, easy to teach/learn, and a lot of fun. I wish I would have come across this game years ago!

More experience with the game may make for a better game, but I'm not eager to play again... (Catch-22).

Acquired May 2007. First play was a three player game with my boys in August 2007. Its a new game for me but it sure seems like a lot of fun. Think this will go over well with my non-gamer extended family. Our first 2 player game with the wife didn't go over well. She agreed to try it again and it went over much better. This is a fun game that has familiar mechanisms of play but has enough variation to make it unique. In fairness, it is an older game to the one I would most compare it too which is Ticket to Ride (card taking to buy tiles {trains} and turns that comprise a single action out of multiple choices. positive.text: Enjoyable tile placement game with a solid puzzle element. Nicely textured with good play mechanics. I could see how some would complain about the solitaire feel of it but our group didn't mind it all. The nature of play lends itself to a casual style of play. To top it off, I like the game's look and the components are good if not incredible.After one play...

We loved this from the very first game. The rules are short, even with lots of examples and illustrations. However, there are always decisions to make. You have to balance between short-term points for set collection and long-term points for tile placement. You have to manage money carefully, as you always need to pay with the correct color of money, and if...

Plus money makes a difference and the walls as well. Just like in the original Alhambra standing in Granada region. Very enjoyable game. I haven't tried the expansions yet, but I will. But some...

Alhambra is an absolute blast! I am not usually a big fan of lighter games, but for some reason, Alhambra is lots of fun. It is easy to teach and play, and yet there is definitely strategy involved. If you like building games, Alhambra is highly recommended. It is one of the few games my mother actually will play and enjoys. It is also a great two player ga...

critical.text: A game that provides a mix of opportunities for good moves and counter-moves. However, the frustrating thing is that they are dependent on the luck of the tile draws and your ability at guessing others tile draws. Against an equally-practiced opponent, this game is no more than a drawn-out crap shoot.

Gave as a gift to a friend based on the "one of the best games since The Sliced Bread Game" concensus on the Geek. Played once, well, not really played so much as went through a game and got the basic gist of how it works. Hope I get to play again, though I will need to learn the rules all over again.

I cannot explain exactly why but I have disliked all my games of this. I just cannot see why this is treated with such reverence on the Geek. The strategy / tactics are at the mercy of the tile draws and other players inadvertent actions. You can effectively be out early on but still have to play on etc. etc. At least it is short :)

This is a solid, good game but it is a real brain burner. Since I only play it once a year or less, I have to re-discover rules and strategy every time I play, so I never do all that well at it. It is one I would play any time, but it's not one that gets suggested very often or that I would probably ever throw on the table. There are just way too many other...

This is a tough one for me. My friends love it and they can't wait to play it. For some reason for me, I have a really hard time 'seeing' what is going on in this game. The board and where you are can change so dynamically that you just can't be attached to anything you have built. Also, I think you really need to be aggressive into breaking into what other...

mixed.text: Waw... I'm deeply impressed with this game. Of all of Knizia's games I have played so far this is the best, and IMO very deservedly in the top 3 here on BBG. Forget the (anti)snobbery, and try to at least play this game once. It had me hooked from the go. Great for 2 as well, regardless of what it says on the side of the Mayfair Edition box, where it incorr...

Muy buen juego y curiosa mecánica, casi abstracto, este hay que explotarlo más! Lo único que le baja la nota a este gran juego es la suerte a la hora de coger o cambiar losetas, que es clave para el juego... Quizás el mejor del prolífero Knizia, que mucho juego, pero pocos que valgan la pena.

Previously owned the board game - now just the iOS version. Certainly a classic game with some ingenious gameplay. If you (or your common play partner(s)) don't like a game where you can take what the other player has built, this is NOT the game for them. My wife was having fun building her little world when I came over and yoinked it from her. She wasn't h...

another game i feel bad giving a rating lower than 8. it's a good game! but, i feel i must be true to the provided BGG rating system which asks not how "great" it is but rather how much i want to play it. well, in theory i want to play it, but in practice the game never comes off the shelf. best i can say is that i'm waiting on someone ELSE to suggest it so...

Easy to play yet very challenging. Lots of strategy involved. Personally I think the rules could have been better written but the game itself is solid. Despite appearances during the game, it's not at all easy to predict who will win. I thought I was kicking butt against my opponents only to find out one of them had one more point than I at the end of the g...

positive.text: Wow. That's the best way to sum up this game. Every time I play, there are so many things I want to do and never get a chance to. I'm always planning what to do next time I play. This is gaming perfection. The opportunities during your turn are so many that I don't think this game will ever be "broken." The difficulty everyone speaks of I never encountered....

Very best modern strategy/tactic game. I love the bit of luck due to tile drawing: balances things out and makes it possible for new or unexperienced players to have fun. One of the rare "almost abstract" multiplayer game that doesn't get chaotic or suffer from the "let's team up and kill Joe" problem.

Was my favorite game for about 6 years. Great strategy. Relatively short. Can play two games in an evening and you feel FULFILLED when you win. This one has it all for me. Great turn angst. Lot's of strategy. Many choices. I love this one even when I lose. However, it has slipped a bit in the last 4 years. Attika and Scythe have replaced it. I guess time ju...

This is a 2 to 4 player tile laying game, where players build up kingdoms of tiles on the board, and try to position their leaders to their best advantage. The game is won by taking cubes in four colours, but your score is the colour you have the least of. Ingenious mechanics and subtle deep game play. Simply wonderful. Buy it now.

This is the best 'German' game of all time, mile better than 'Puerto Rico' for a start! T+E is fantastic in that there is always something a player can do to improve their situation regardless of the tiles in hand or the situation on the board. Thus the element of luck in the game (the drawing of tiles) is balanced by the relative freedom to put those tiles...
